\begin{definitionv}{synth_8}[Admissible three-way split]
At sample size \(n\), an admissible three-way split is a deterministic triple \(B_n=(I_0,I_1,I_2)\) of pairwise-disjoint subsets of \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\) such that \(|I_j|\geq\lfloor n/4\rfloor\) for \(j=0,1,2\). The blocks are fixed before observing the sample.
\end{definitionv}

\begin{definitionv}{synth_16}[Independent product sample laws]
For an observed-data law \(P\) on \(\mathcal X\times[0,1]\times[0,1]\), write \(P^{\otimes n}\) for the \(n\)-fold product law governing the observed sample \((O_1,\ldots,O_n)\), under which the coordinates are independent with common law \(P\). For a full-data law package \(P^{\mathrm F}\), write \((P^{\mathrm F})^{\otimes n}\) for the \(n\)-fold product law governing \(n\) independent full-data draws from \(P^{\mathrm F}\); estimators and intervals indexed by this law are measurable functions of the induced observed coordinates \((O_1,\ldots,O_n)\).
\end{definitionv}

\begin{assumptionv}{ass:iid-sampling}[I.i.d. sampling]
The observed units \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent and identically distributed according to \(P\).
\end{assumptionv}

\begin{assumptionv}{ass:conditional-density-law}[Conditional treatment density]
For each \(x\in\mathcal X\), the map \(a\mapsto \pi_x(a)\) is Borel measurable on \([0,1]\), and \(\pi_x(a)\ge 0\) for Lebesgue-a.e. \(a\in[0,1]\). Moreover, \(p_x=P(X=x)\), and for every Borel set \(B\subseteq[0,1]\),
\[
P(X=x,\ A\in B)=p_x\int_B \pi_x(a)\,\mathrm da .
\]
\end{assumptionv}

\begin{assumptionv}{ass:stratum-mass}[Stratum mass lower bound]
For every \(x\in\mathcal X\),
\[
p_x\geq p_{\min}.
\]
\end{assumptionv}

\begin{assumptionv}{ass:polynomial-thinning}[Polynomial overlap thinning]
For every \(x\in\mathcal X\) and for Lebesgue-almost every \(a\in[0,1]\),
\[
c_- a^\kappa \leq \pi_x(a) \leq c_+ a^\kappa .
\]
\end{assumptionv}

\begin{definitionv}{synth_19}[Local-polynomial degree]
For each smoothness exponent \(\beta\in\mathbb R\), the local-polynomial degree is
\[
\ell(\beta):=\max\{\lceil\beta\rceil_{\mathbb N}-1,0\},
\]
where \(\lceil\beta\rceil_{\mathbb N}\) denotes the least natural number greater than or equal to \(\beta\).
\end{definitionv}

\begin{assumptionv}{ass:holder-regression}[Hölder regression regularity]
The regression function \(\mu_x^P\) satisfies the following condition with parameters \(\beta\) and \(L\). For every \(x\in\mathcal X\):
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Continuity.)} The map \(a\mapsto \mu_x^P(a)\) is continuous on \([0,1]\).
\item \textbf{(Range.)} For every \(a\in[0,1]\), \(\mu_x^P(a)\in[0,1]\).
\item \textbf{(Regression version.)} The function \(\mu_X^P(A)\) realizes the conditional outcome regression given the complete design:
\[
\mathbb E_P[Y\mid X,A]=\mu_X^P(A)
\quad P\text{-almost surely}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Hölder Taylor remainder.)} Let \(\ell=\ell(\beta)\) be the local-polynomial order defined in \cref{obj:synth_19}. For all \(s,t\in[0,1]\), with derivatives taken intrinsically on \([0,1]\),
\[
\left|
\mu_x^P(t)
-
\sum_{j=0}^{\ell}
\frac{(\mu_x^P)^{(j)}(s)}{j!}(t-s)^j
\right|
\le
L|t-s|^\beta .
\]
\end{itemize}
\end{assumptionv}

\begin{definitionv}{synth_18}[Observed continuity class $\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}$]
Let \(\mathcal X=\{1,\ldots,J\}\), let \(O=(X,A,Y)\in\mathcal X\times[0,1]\times[0,1]\), and let \(P\in\mathcal P(\mathcal X\times[0,1]\times[0,1])\). Write
\[
p_x=P(X=x).
\]
The law \(P\) belongs to the continuity-only class \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}\) when, for every \(x\in\mathcal X\), the conditional-density condition of \cref{obj:ass:conditional-density-law}, the stratum-mass condition of \cref{obj:ass:stratum-mass}, and the polynomial-thinning condition of \cref{obj:ass:polynomial-thinning} hold, and an almost-everywhere version of \(a\mapsto\mathbb E_P[Y\mid A=a,X=x]\) has a unique continuous extension
\[
\mu_{x,\mathrm{cont}}^P:[0,\bar\delta]\to[0,1].
\]
The Hölder class \(\mathcal M\) imposes the same three design conditions together with the Hölder regression condition of \cref{obj:ass:holder-regression}; its canonical definition is \cref{obj:def:model-class}, and the canonical continuity-only definition is \cref{obj:def:continuity-model-class}.
\end{definitionv}

\begin{definitionv}{def:model-class}[Observed law class \(\mathcal M\)]
For \(P\in\mathcal P(\mathcal X\times[0,1]\times[0,1])\), let
\[
p_x=P(X=x),
\qquad x\in\mathcal X .
\]
The observed-data law class \(\mathcal M\) is
\[
\mathcal M
=
\left\{
P\in\mathcal P(\mathcal X\times[0,1]\times[0,1])
:
P\text{ satisfies the conditions listed below}
\right\}.
\]
Membership means that \(P\) satisfies:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Conditional density.)} The conditional-density condition in \cref{obj:ass:conditional-density-law}.
\item \textbf{(Stratum mass.)} The stratum-mass condition in \cref{obj:ass:stratum-mass}.
\item \textbf{(Polynomial thinning.)} The polynomial-thinning condition in \cref{obj:ass:polynomial-thinning}.
\item \textbf{(Hölder regression.)} The Hölder member condition in \cref{obj:ass:holder-regression}.
\end{itemize}
\end{definitionv}

\begin{definitionv}{def:clamp-policy}[Clamp policy \(d_\delta\) and \(A^\delta\)]
For \(0\leq\delta\leq\bar\delta\), the lower-threshold clamp map \(d_\delta\) and the clamped treatment \(A^\delta\) are
\[
d_\delta(a)=\max\{a,\delta\},
\qquad
A^\delta=d_\delta(A).
\]
\end{definitionv}

\begin{definitionv}{def:clamp-functional}[Clamp functionals \(q_x(\delta)\), \(\nu_\delta(P)\), and \(\theta_\delta(P)\)]
For \(P\in\mathcal M\) as in \cref{obj:def:model-class}, \(x\in\mathcal X\), and \(0\leq\delta\leq\bar\delta\), define
\[
q_x(\delta)=\int_{[0,\delta]}\pi_x(a)\,\mathrm da,
\qquad
\nu_\delta(P)=\mathbb E_P\!\left[Y\mathbf 1\{A>\delta\}\right].
\]
The unsmoothed observed-data clamp target is
\[
\theta_\delta(P)
=
\nu_\delta(P)
+
\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p_xq_x(\delta)\mu_x^P(\delta).
\]
\end{definitionv}

\begin{definitionv}{def:bandwidth}[Information-balance bandwidth \(h_n\)]
The information-balance bandwidth \(h_n\) for the threshold sequence \(\delta_n\) is
\[
h_n
=
\inf\left\{
h\in(0,1-\bar\delta]:
n h^{2\beta+1}(\delta_n+h)^\kappa\geq 1
\right\},
\]
with \(h_n=1-\bar\delta\) when the displayed set is empty.
\end{definitionv}

\begin{definitionv}{def:frontier}[Frontier rate \(r_n\)]
The Hölder minimax rate \(r_n\) is
\[
r_n=n^{-1/2}+\delta_n^{\kappa+1}h_n^\beta .
\]
\end{definitionv}

\begin{definitionv}{synth_6}[Projection onto the outcome range]
For a real number \(t\), define \(\Pi_{[0,1]}(t)=\min\{1,\max\{0,t\}\}\). Applied to an estimator or interval endpoint, \(\Pi_{[0,1]}\) denotes this pointwise projection onto the outcome range \([0,1]\).
\end{definitionv}

\begin{definitionv}{synth_2}[Continuity-only regression extension]
For \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}\) and \(x\in\mathcal X\), \(\mu_{x,\mathrm{cont}}^P\) denotes the unique continuous function on \([0,\bar\delta]\) that agrees, almost everywhere on that interval under the conditional treatment law given \(X=x\), with a version of the conditional mean \(a\mapsto\mathbb E_P[Y\mid A=a,X=x]\).
\end{definitionv}

\begin{definitionv}{def:local-design-notation}[Local design notation]
For a realized sample \(z=(O_1,\ldots,O_n)\), deterministic split blocks \(I_0,I_1,I_2\) as in \cref{obj:synth_8}, a stratum \(x\in\mathcal X\), local-polynomial degree \(\ell\), threshold \(\delta_n\), and bandwidth \(h_n\), put
\[
U_i=\frac{A_i-\delta_n}{h_n},
\qquad
v_\ell(u)=(1,u,\ldots,u^\ell)^\top .
\]
Define
\[
N_x
=
\sum_{i\in I_2}\mathbf 1\{X_i=x,\ A_i\in[\delta_n,\delta_n+h_n]\}
\]
and
\[
G_x
=
\sum_{i\in I_2}
\mathbf 1\{X_i=x,\ 0\leq U_i\leq1\}
v_\ell(U_i)v_\ell(U_i)^\top .
\]
For \(\rho\geq0\), define
\[
M_{\ell,\kappa,\rho}
=
\frac{\int_0^1v_\ell(u)v_\ell(u)^\top(\rho+u)^\kappa\,\mathrm du}
{\int_0^1(\rho+u)^\kappa\,\mathrm du},
\]
and set
\[
\lambda_\star
=
\frac{c_-}{c_+}
\inf_{\rho\geq0}
\lambda_{\min}\!\left(M_{\ell,\kappa,\rho}\right).
\]
The good-design event \(\Omega_x\) is the event that \(N_x>0\) and, for every \(v\in\mathbb R^{\ell+1}\),
\[
v^\top G_xv
\geq
\frac{\lambda_\star N_x}{2}\lVert v\rVert_2^2 .
\]
The exact local-polynomial intercept weight is
\[
w_{ix}
=
\begin{cases}
\mathbf 1\{i\in I_2,\ X_i=x,\ 0\leq U_i\leq1\}\,
e_0^\top G_x^{-1}v_\ell(U_i),
& \text{on }\Omega_x,\\
0, & \text{on }\Omega_x^c .
\end{cases}
\]
\end{definitionv}

\begin{algorithmv}{def:total-gram-estimator}[Total-Gram estimator \(\widehat\theta_n\)]
Given split blocks \(I_0,I_1,I_2\) and the local-design quantities in \cref{obj:def:local-design-notation}, define the estimator as follows.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Compute the retained-course empirical mean
\[
\widehat\nu_n
=
\frac{1}{|I_0|}
\sum_{i\in I_0}Y_i\mathbf 1\{A_i>\delta_n\}.
\]
\item For each \(x\in\mathcal X\), compute the empirical lower-threshold atom mass
\[
\widehat b_x
=
\frac{1}{|I_1|}
\sum_{i\in I_1}\mathbf 1\{X_i=x,\ A_i\leq\delta_n\}.
\]
\item For each \(x\in\mathcal X\), compute the clipped local-polynomial threshold estimate
\[
\widetilde\mu_x
=
\begin{cases}
\Pi_{[0,1]}\!\left(\sum_{i\in I_2}w_{ix}Y_i\right),& \Omega_x,\\
1/2,& \Omega_x^{c}.
\end{cases}
\]
\item Output the total-Gram clamp-target estimator
\[
\widehat\theta_n
=
\Pi_{[0,1]}\!\left[
\widehat\nu_n+\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}\widehat b_x\widetilde\mu_x
\right].
\]
\end{enumerate}
\end{algorithmv}

\begin{algorithmv}{def:honest-interval}[Honest interval \(\mathrm{CI}_n\)]
Given the local-design quantities in \cref{obj:def:local-design-notation}, define the interval as follows.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Set the Hoeffding calibration multiplier and split-block stochastic-error radii
\[
t_\alpha=\sqrt{\frac{\log(12J/\alpha)}{2}},
\qquad
b_0=\frac{t_\alpha}{\sqrt{|I_0|}},
\qquad
b_1=\frac{t_\alpha}{\sqrt{|I_1|}}.
\]
\item For each \(x\in\mathcal X\), set the local regression bias-plus-noise radius
\[
B_x
=
Lh_n^\beta\sum_{i\in I_2}|w_{ix}|
+
t_\alpha\left(\sum_{i\in I_2}w_{ix}^2\right)^{1/2}.
\]
\item For each \(x\in\mathcal X\), set the atom-weighted interval contribution
\[
D_x
=
\begin{cases}
(\widehat b_x+b_1)B_x+b_1,& \Omega_x,\\
\widehat b_x+b_1,& \Omega_x^{c}.
\end{cases}
\]
\item Output the bias-aware honest interval
\[
\mathrm{CI}_n
=
\left[
\widehat\theta_n-b_0-\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}D_x,\,
\widehat\theta_n+b_0+\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}D_x
\right]\cap[0,1].
\]
\end{enumerate}
\end{algorithmv}

\begin{definitionv}{synth_4}[Total-Gram stabilized estimator]
Let \(B_n=(I_{0,n},I_{1,n},I_{2,n})\) be a deterministic admissible three-way split, let \(h_n\) be the information-balance bandwidth, and let \(\ell\) be the local-polynomial order. Define the projection
\[
  \operatorname{clamp}_{[0,1]}(t)=\min\{1,\max\{0,t\}\}.
\]
Set
\[
  \widehat\nu_n=|I_{0,n}|^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_{0,n}}Y_i\mathbf 1\{A_i>\delta_n\},\qquad
  \widehat b_x=|I_{1,n}|^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_{1,n}}\mathbf 1\{X_i=x,A_i\le\delta_n\}.
\]
For each \(x\), let \(\widetilde\mu_x=\operatorname{clamp}_{[0,1]}(\sum_{i\in I_{2,n}}w_{ix}Y_i)\) on \(\Omega_x\), and let \(\widetilde\mu_x=1/2\) on \(\Omega_x^c\). The split-indexed total-Gram estimator is
\[
  \widehat\theta_{n,B_n}^{\mathrm{TG}}
  =\operatorname{clamp}_{[0,1]}\!\left(\widehat\nu_n+\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}\widehat b_x\widetilde\mu_x\right).
\]
\end{definitionv}

\begin{definitionv}{synth_12}[Bias-aware interval for a fixed split $B_n$]
Let $B_n=(I_{0,n},I_{1,n},I_{2,n})$ be an admissible deterministic three-way split at sample size $n$. With $h_n$ and $\delta_n$ fixed, form the total-Gram weights $w_{ix}$ and good-design events $\Omega_x$ from the third block $I_{2,n}$. Set $\widehat\nu_{n,B_n}=|I_{0,n}|^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_{0,n}}Y_i\mathbf 1\{A_i>\delta_n\}$, $\widehat b_{x,B_n}=|I_{1,n}|^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_{1,n}}\mathbf 1\{X_i=x,A_i\leq\delta_n\}$, and $\widetilde\mu_{x,B_n}=\Pi_{[0,1]}(\sum_{i\in I_{2,n}}w_{ix}Y_i)$ on $\Omega_x$, with $\widetilde\mu_{x,B_n}=1/2$ on $\Omega_x^c$. Define $\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{TG}}_{n,B_n}=\Pi_{[0,1]}\{\widehat\nu_{n,B_n}+\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}\widehat b_{x,B_n}\widetilde\mu_{x,B_n}\}$. Let $t_\alpha=\sqrt{\log(12J/\alpha)/2}$, $b_{0,B_n}=t_\alpha/\sqrt{|I_{0,n}|}$, and $b_{1,B_n}=t_\alpha/\sqrt{|I_{1,n}|}$. For each $x\in\mathcal X$, set $B_{x,B_n}=Lh_n^\beta\sum_{i\in I_{2,n}}|w_{ix}|+t_\alpha(\sum_{i\in I_{2,n}}w_{ix}^2)^{1/2}$ and $D_{x,B_n}=(\widehat b_{x,B_n}+b_{1,B_n})B_{x,B_n}+b_{1,B_n}$ on $\Omega_x$, while $D_{x,B_n}=\widehat b_{x,B_n}+b_{1,B_n}$ on $\Omega_x^c$. The bias-aware interval formed from $B_n$ is $\mathrm{CI}_{n,B_n}=[\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{TG}}_{n,B_n}-b_{0,B_n}-\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}D_{x,B_n},\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{TG}}_{n,B_n}+b_{0,B_n}+\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}D_{x,B_n}]\cap[0,1]$.
\end{definitionv}

\begin{definitionv}{synth_17}[Length of an observed-sample interval]
For an observed-sample measurable interval \(C_n=C_n(O_1,\ldots,O_n)=[\ell_n(O_1,\ldots,O_n),u_n(O_1,\ldots,O_n)]\subseteq[0,1]\), define its length pointwise by \(\operatorname{len}(C_n)=u_n(O_1,\ldots,O_n)-\ell_n(O_1,\ldots,O_n)\). Thus expected lengths such as \(\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}[\operatorname{len}(C_n)]\) are taken with respect to the \(n\)-fold observed-sample law.
\end{definitionv}

\begin{definitionv}{synth_5}[Concrete stabilized risk and length]
For a deterministic admissible split \(B_n\), define the finite-sample worst-case risk of the total-Gram estimator by
\[
  \operatorname{Risk}_n(B_n)=\sup_{P\in\mathcal M}
  \mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}\!\left|\widehat\theta_{n,B_n}^{\mathrm{TG}}-\theta_{\delta_n}(P)\right|.
\]
For the bias-aware interval \(\mathrm{CI}_{n,B_n}\) formed from the same split, define its worst-case expected length by
\[
  \operatorname{Length}_n(B_n)=\sup_{P\in\mathcal M}
  \mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}[\operatorname{len}(\mathrm{CI}_{n,B_n})].
\]
\end{definitionv}

\begin{definitionv}{synth_10}[One-cell Bernoulli regressions]
In the one-stratum calibration with \(\beta=\kappa=1\) and \(\pi(a)=2a\), define the null Bernoulli regression by \(m_0(a)=1/2\). For a threshold \(\delta_n\) and bandwidth \(h_n>0\), define the localized alternative by \(m_{1,\delta_n,h_n}(a)=1/2+h_n\,\tau_{\delta_n,h_n}(a)\), where \(\tau_{\delta,h}(a)=\max\{0,1-|a-\delta|/h\}\).
\end{definitionv}

\begin{definitionv}{synth_3}[Observed minimax risk and honest length]
For the observed clamp target \(\theta_{\delta_n}(P)\) over \(\mathcal M\), the minimax absolute-error risk is
\[
  R_n^\star=\inf_{\widehat\theta}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M}
  \mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}\!\left|\widehat\theta(O_1,\ldots,O_n)-\theta_{\delta_n}(P)\right|,
\]
where the infimum ranges over observed-sample measurable estimators taking values in \([0,1]\). The minimax honest expected length is
\[
  L_n^\star=\inf_{C_n:\,\inf_{P\in\mathcal M}P^{\otimes n}\{\theta_{\delta_n}(P)\in C_n\}\ge 1-\alpha}
  \sup_{P\in\mathcal M}\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}[\operatorname{len}(C_n)],
\]
where \(C_n\) ranges over observed-sample measurable interval procedures with endpoints in \([0,1]\).
\end{definitionv}

\begin{theoremv}{thm:minimax-risk}[Minimax clamp frontier]
Fix \(J,\beta,\kappa,L,c_-,c_+,p_{\min},\bar\delta,\alpha\) satisfying the regime conditions:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Regime.)} \(J\geq 1\), \(\beta>0\), \(\kappa\geq0\), \(L>0\), \(c_->0\), \(c_-\leq \kappa+1\leq c_+\), \(p_{\min}>0\), \(p_{\min}\leq 1/J\), \(\bar\delta\in(0,1)\), and \(\alpha\in(0,1/2)\).
\end{itemize}
Then there exist constants \(0<c<C\) and an amplitude \(a\in(0,1/4]\), depending only on the displayed regime constants, such that, for every deterministic threshold sequence \((\delta_n)_{n\geq1}\) with \(\delta_n\in[0,\bar\delta]\) for every \(n\) and every deterministic sequence \(B_n=(I_{0,n},I_{1,n},I_{2,n})\) of three pairwise-disjoint sample blocks with \(|I_{j,n}|\geq \lfloor n/4\rfloor\) for \(j=0,1,2\), for all sufficiently large \(n\), with \(h_n\) the information-balance bandwidth from \cref{obj:def:bandwidth} and
\[
r_n=n^{-1/2}+\delta_n^{\kappa+1}h_n^\beta
\]
as in \cref{obj:def:frontier}, the observed minimax absolute-error risk \(R_n^\star\) over the clamp model \(\mathcal M\) in \cref{obj:def:model-class} and the worst-case i.i.d. risk over \(\mathcal M\) of the stabilized estimator using \(B_n\) satisfy
\[
c r_n
\leq
R_n^\star
\leq
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M} \mathbb E_P\!\left[
\left|\widehat\theta_{n,B_n}^{\mathrm{TG}}-\theta_{\delta_n}(P)\right|
\right]
\leq
C r_n .
\]
Moreover, for all sufficiently large \(n\), the lower bound is witnessed inside the same clamp model by:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Global shift.)} Laws \(P_0,P_1\in\mathcal M\) satisfying \cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling}, with the same \((X,A)\)-design distribution and the same \(p_x\) and \(\pi_x\) functions, having Bernoulli outcomes, and obeying
\[
\mu_x^{P_1}(a)=\mu_x^{P_0}(a)+n^{-1/2}
\quad\text{for every }x\text{ and }a\in[0,1],
\]
with well-posed product chi-squared divergence,
\[
P_1^{\otimes n}\ll P_0^{\otimes n},
\qquad
\int \left(\frac{dP_1^{\otimes n}}{dP_0^{\otimes n}}-1\right)^2\,dP_0^{\otimes n}<\infty,
\]
and
\[
c n^{-1/2}
\leq
\left|\theta_{\delta_n}(P_1)-\theta_{\delta_n}(P_0)\right|,
\qquad
\chi^2\!\left(P_1^{\otimes n},P_0^{\otimes n}\right)\leq C .
\]
\item \textbf{(Localized perturbation.)} Laws \(Q_0,Q_1\in\mathcal M\) satisfying \cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling}, with the same \((X,A)\)-design distribution and the same \(p_x\) and \(\pi_x\) functions, having Bernoulli outcomes, and admitting a continuous bump \(b:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) satisfying \(b(0)=1\), \(b(u)\geq0\) for every \(u\), \(b(u)=0\) for \(u\notin[-1,1]\), and \(|b(u)|\leq1\) for \(u\in[-1,1]\), with regression shift
\[
\mu_x^{Q_1}(t)-\mu_x^{Q_0}(t)
=
a\,h_n^\beta b\!\left(\frac{t-\delta_n}{h_n}\right)
\]
for every \(x\) and \(t\in[0,1]\). The product chi-squared divergence is well posed,
\[
Q_1^{\otimes n}\ll Q_0^{\otimes n},
\qquad
\int \left(\frac{dQ_1^{\otimes n}}{dQ_0^{\otimes n}}-1\right)^2\,dQ_0^{\otimes n}<\infty,
\]
and
\[
c\,\delta_n^{\kappa+1}h_n^\beta
\leq
\left|\theta_{\delta_n}(Q_1)-\theta_{\delta_n}(Q_0)\right|,
\qquad
\chi^2\!\left(Q_1^{\otimes n},Q_0^{\otimes n}\right)\leq C .
\]
\end{itemize}
\end{theoremv}

\begin{theoremv}{thm:honest-length}[Honest length frontier]
There are constants \(c,C\in(0,\infty)\), with \(c<C\), for which the following holds.

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Regime constants.)} The number of strata \(J\) is a positive integer, \(\beta>0\), \(\kappa\geq0\), \(L>0\), \(c_->0\), \(c_-\leq \kappa+1\leq c_+\), \(p_{\min}>0\), \(p_{\min}\leq 1/J\), \(\bar\delta\in(0,1)\), and \(\alpha\in(0,1/2)\).
\item \textbf{(Threshold path.)} The deterministic thresholds satisfy \(0\leq \delta_n\leq \bar\delta\) for every \(n\).
\item \textbf{(Sample splits.)} For every \(n\), \(B_n=(I_{0,n},I_{1,n},I_{2,n})\) is a deterministic three-way split of the sample indices with pairwise disjoint blocks and \(|I_{j,n}|\geq \lfloor n/4\rfloor\) for \(j=0,1,2\).
\end{itemize}

For all sufficiently large \(n\), set \(h_n\) to be the information-balance bandwidth for \(\delta_n\) from \cref{obj:def:bandwidth}, and set
\[
r_n=n^{-1/2}+\delta_n^{\kappa+1}h_n^\beta .
\]
Then the stabilized interval \(\mathrm{CI}_n\) has worst-case coverage
\[
\inf\Bigl\{
P^{\otimes n}\{\theta_{\delta_n}(P)\in \mathrm{CI}_n(O_1,\ldots,O_n)\}:
P\in\mathcal M
\Bigr\}\geq 1-\alpha,
\]
and its worst-case expected length is comparable to \(r_n\):
\[
c\,r_n
\leq
\sup\Bigl\{
\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}\bigl[\operatorname{len}(\mathrm{CI}_n)\bigr]:
P\in\mathcal M
\Bigr\}
\leq
C\,r_n .
\]
Moreover, the minimax honest expected length satisfies
\[
c\,r_n
\leq
L_n^\star,
\]
where \(L_n^\star\) is the infimum, over observed-sample confidence procedures with uniform coverage at least \(1-\alpha\) over \(\mathcal M\), of their worst-case expected length. Equivalently, every observed-sample confidence procedure \(C_n\) with
\[
\inf\Bigl\{
P^{\otimes n}\{\theta_{\delta_n}(P)\in C_n(O_1,\ldots,O_n)\}:
P\in\mathcal M
\Bigr\}\geq 1-\alpha
\]
has worst-case expected length at least \(c\,r_n\):
\[
c\,r_n
\leq
\sup\Bigl\{
\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}\bigl[\operatorname{len}(C_n)\bigr]:
P\in\mathcal M
\Bigr\}.
\]
\end{theoremv}

\begin{theoremv}{thm:phase-diagram}[Phase boundary regimes]
Let \(J\) be a positive integer and let
\[
\beta>0,\qquad
\kappa\geq 0,\qquad
L>0,\qquad
0<c_-\leq \kappa+1\leq c_+,\qquad
0<p_{\min}\leq 1/J,\qquad
0<\bar\delta<1,\qquad
0<\alpha<1/2 .
\]
Define the phase and edge scales by
\[
\delta_{\mathrm{crit},n}
=
n^{-1/\{2(\beta\kappa+2\beta+\kappa+1)\}},
\qquad
\delta_{\mathrm{edge},n}
=
n^{-1/(2\beta+\kappa+1)} .
\]
Then
\[
\frac{\delta_{\mathrm{crit},n}}{\delta_{\mathrm{edge},n}}\to\infty .
\]
Moreover, for every deterministic threshold sequence \((\delta_n)_{n\geq 1}\) with \(\delta_n\in[0,\bar\delta]\) for every \(n\), let \(h_n\) be the information-balance bandwidth in \cref{obj:def:bandwidth}, and set
\[
a_n=\delta_n^{\kappa+1}h_n^\beta,
\qquad
r_n=n^{-1/2}+\delta_n^{\kappa+1}h_n^\beta
\]
as in \cref{obj:def:frontier}. The following conclusions hold:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Regular thresholds.} If \(\delta_n/\delta_{\mathrm{crit},n}\to 0\), then \(r_n\asymp n^{-1/2}\).
\item \textbf{Critical thresholds.} For every \(c_0>0\), if \(\delta_n/\delta_{\mathrm{crit},n}\to c_0\), then \(a_n\asymp n^{-1/2}\) and \(r_n\asymp n^{-1/2}\).
\item \textbf{Vanishing atom-dominated thresholds.} If \(\delta_n/\delta_{\mathrm{crit},n}\to\infty\) and \(\delta_n\to0\), then
\[
r_n\asymp
\delta_n^{\kappa+1}\bigl(n\delta_n^\kappa\bigr)^{-\beta/(2\beta+1)} .
\]
\item \textbf{Fixed thresholds.} For every \(\delta_0\in(0,\bar\delta]\), if \(\delta_n\to\delta_0\), then
\[
r_n\asymp n^{-\beta/(2\beta+1)} .
\]
\item \textbf{Zero threshold identities.} For every \(n\) and every \(P\in\mathcal M\) satisfying \cref{obj:def:model-class},
\[
q_x(0)=0\quad\text{for every }x,\qquad
\theta_0(P)=\int Y\,dP,\qquad
r_n\big|_{\delta_n=0}=n^{-1/2},
\]
where the last identity uses the bandwidth \(h_n\) at threshold \(0\).
\item \textbf{Zero threshold estimator.} For every \(n\), every \(P\in\mathcal M\) satisfying \cref{obj:def:model-class}, and every admissible three-way split \(B=(I_0,I_1,I_2)\) as in \cref{obj:def:total-gram-estimator}, the total-Gram estimator in \cref{obj:def:total-gram-estimator}, formed at threshold \(0\) with bandwidth \(h_n\), agrees under the product sampling law generated by \(P\) with
\[
z\mapsto
\operatorname{clamp}_{[0,1]}\!\left(\frac{1}{|I_0|}\sum_{i\in I_0}Y_i\right).
\]
\item \textbf{Zero threshold stabilized guarantees.} For every deterministic sequence \(B_\bullet=(B_n)_{n\geq1}\) of admissible three-way split blocks, the stabilized zero-threshold procedure has coverage at least \(1-\alpha\) for all sufficiently large \(n\). Its stabilized worst-case risk at threshold \(0\) and its stabilized worst-case expected length at threshold \(0\) with noncoverage level \(\alpha\) are both asymptotic to \(n^{-1/2}\).
\end{itemize}
\end{theoremv}

\begin{propositionv}{prop:one-cell-calibration}[One-cell calibration]
Let \(\bar\delta\in(0,1)\), and let \((\delta_n)_{n\geq1}\) be a deterministic threshold sequence satisfying
\[
0\leq \delta_n\leq \bar\delta
\qquad\text{for every }n .
\]
Assume that \(\delta_n\gg n^{-1/4}\), in the sense that
\[
\frac{\delta_n}{n^{-1/4}}\longrightarrow\infty .
\]
In the one-stratum model with \(\beta=\kappa=1\) and \(\pi(a)=2a\), let \(h_n\) be the information-balance bandwidth from \cref{obj:def:bandwidth} evaluated at \((\delta_n,1,1,\bar\delta)\). For the concrete localized Bernoulli alternatives, define
\[
K_n
=
n\int_0^1
\operatorname{KL}\!\left(
\operatorname{Bernoulli}(m_{1,\delta_n,h_n}(a)),
\operatorname{Bernoulli}(m_0(a))
\right)\,2a\,da
\]
and
\[
\Delta_n
=
\int_{\delta_n}^1
\bigl(m_{1,\delta_n,h_n}(a)-m_0(a)\bigr)\,2a\,da
+
\left(\int_0^{\delta_n}2a\,da\right)
\bigl(m_{1,\delta_n,h_n}(\delta_n)-m_0(\delta_n)\bigr).
\]
Then
\[
h_n\asymp (n\delta_n)^{-1/3},
\qquad
K_n\asymp n\delta_n h_n^3,
\qquad
\Delta_n\asymp \delta_n^2h_n.
\]
Moreover,
\[
\delta_n\asymp n^{-1/10}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\Delta_n\asymp n^{-1/2}.
\]
\end{propositionv}

\begin{assumptionv}{ass:consistency}[Structural consistency]
Under \(P^{\mathrm F}\), the following conditions hold:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Latent response.)} The latent response variable \(U\) takes values in \(\mathcal U\).
\item \textbf{(Structural maps.)} For every \(x\in\mathcal X\), the map
\[
g_x:[0,1]\times\mathcal U\to[0,1]
\]
is jointly Borel measurable.
\item \textbf{(Potential and observed outcomes.)} There is a single \(P^{\mathrm F}\)-null set outside which, for every \(a\in[0,1]\),
\[
Y(a)=g_X(a,U),
\qquad
Y=g_X(A,U).
\]
\end{itemize}
\end{assumptionv}

\begin{assumptionv}{ass:exchangeability}[Conditional exchangeability]
Under \(P^{\mathrm F}\), the treatment \(A\) and latent response variable \(U\) are conditionally independent given \(X\).
\end{assumptionv}

\begin{definitionv}{synth_1}[Full-data response mean]
For a full-data law package \(P^{\mathrm F}\) with latent-response carrier \(\mathcal U\), latent variable \(U\), structural maps \(g_x:[0,1]\times\mathcal U\to[0,1]\), and observed stratum \(X\), the full-data response mean in stratum \(x\in\mathcal X\) is
\[
  m_x^{\mathrm F}(a)=\mathbb E_{P^{\mathrm F}}\{g_x(a,U)\mid X=x\},\qquad a\in[0,1].
\]
When the law package is in the full-data continuity model, the map \(a\mapsto m_x^{\mathrm F}(a)\) is continuous on \([0,\bar\delta]\) for every \(x\in\mathcal X\).
\end{definitionv}

\begin{assumptionv}{ass:full-data-response-continuity}[Full-data response continuity]
Under the full-data law \(P^{\mathrm F}\), for every \(x\in\mathcal X\), the full-data response mean \(a\mapsto m_x^{\mathrm F}(a)\) is continuous on \([0,\bar\delta]\).
\end{assumptionv}

\begin{definitionv}{def:full-data-model-class}[Full-data causal class \(\mathcal M^{\mathrm F}\)]
\(\mathcal M^{\mathrm F}\) is the collection of full-data law packages \(P^{\mathrm F}\) satisfying the following memberwise structure relative to \cref{obj:def:model-class,obj:ass:consistency,obj:ass:exchangeability,obj:ass:full-data-response-continuity}.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Latent response space.)} Each member carries its own standard Borel latent-response space \(\mathcal U\) and an \(\mathcal U\)-valued random variable \(U\).
\item \textbf{(Structural response maps.)} Each member carries jointly Borel maps
\[
g_x:[0,1]\times\mathcal U\to[0,1],
\qquad x\in\mathcal X,
\]
and a jointly measurable potential-outcome process
\[
\{Y(a):a\in[0,1]\}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Full-data law.)} Each member carries a probability law for
\[
(X,A,Y,U,\{Y(a):a\in[0,1]\}).
\]
\item \textbf{(Observed margin.)} The \((X,A,Y)\)-margin is some \(P\in\mathcal M\).
\item \textbf{(Causal member conditions.)} Within the member's own carrier, the simultaneous latent-response consistency, latent randomization, and fiberwise structural-mean continuity on \([0,\bar\delta]\) conditions hold.
\end{itemize}
The class is formed member by member, with membership determined on each member's own standard Borel carrier.
\end{definitionv}

\begin{definitionv}{def:causal-clamp-mean}[Causal clamp mean \(\psi_\delta(P^{\mathrm F})\)]
For a full-data law \(P^{\mathrm F}\) as in \cref{obj:def:full-data-model-class}, the clamp policy \(d_\delta\) from \cref{obj:def:clamp-policy}, and \(0\leq\delta\leq\bar\delta\), define the causal clamp mean by
\[
\psi_\delta(P^{\mathrm F})
=
\mathbb E_{P^{\mathrm F}}\!\left[Y(d_\delta(A))\right].
\]
\end{definitionv}

\begin{definitionv}{def:causal-frontier-criteria}[Causal frontier criteria \(R_{n,\mathrm F}^\star\) and \(L_{n,\mathrm F}^\star\)]
For the causal clamp mean in \cref{obj:def:causal-clamp-mean}, define the causal minimax absolute-error risk over estimators measurable with respect to the observed sample \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) by
\[
 R_{n,\mathrm F}^\star
 =
 \inf_{\widehat\psi}\sup_{P^{\mathrm F}\in\mathcal M^{\mathrm F}}
 \mathbb E_{(P^{\mathrm F})^{\otimes n}}
 \left|\widehat\psi-\psi_{\delta_n}(P^{\mathrm F})\right|.
\]
For intervals \(C_n\) measurable with respect to the same observed sample, define the causal minimax honest expected length by
\[
 L_{n,\mathrm F}^\star
 =
 \inf_{C_n:\,\inf_{P^{\mathrm F}\in\mathcal M^{\mathrm F}}
 (P^{\mathrm F})^{\otimes n}
 \left\{\psi_{\delta_n}(P^{\mathrm F})\in C_n\right\}\geq1-\alpha}
 \sup_{P^{\mathrm F}\in\mathcal M^{\mathrm F}}
 \mathbb E_{(P^{\mathrm F})^{\otimes n}}
 \left[\operatorname{len}(C_n)\right].
\]
\end{definitionv}

\begin{propositionv}{prop:causal-bridge}[Causal bridge identity]
Let \(P^{\mathrm F}\in\mathcal M^{\mathrm F}\) satisfy \cref{obj:def:full-data-model-class}, let \(P\) be its observed \((X,A,Y)\)-margin, and let \(d_\delta(a)=\max\{a,\delta\}\) be the clamp map in \cref{obj:def:clamp-policy}.  Suppose the frontier constants satisfy
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Strata.)} \(J\geq 1\).
\item \textbf{(Smoothness and thinning.)} \(\beta>0\), \(\kappa\geq 0\), and \(L>0\).
\item \textbf{(Density and mass constants.)} \(c_->0\), \(c_-\leq \kappa+1\leq c_+\), \(p_{\min}>0\), and \(p_{\min}\leq 1/J\).
\item \textbf{(Threshold and coverage levels.)} \(0<\bar\delta<1\) and \(0<\alpha<1/2\).
\end{itemize}
For \(x\in\mathcal X\) and \(a\in[0,1]\), define the full-data response mean
\[
m_x^{\mathrm F}(a)
=
P^{\mathrm F}(X=x)^{-1}
\int_{\{X=x\}} g_x(a,U)\,dP^{\mathrm F}.
\]
Then, for every \(x\in\mathcal X\) and every Borel set \(B\subseteq[0,1]\),
\[
P(X=x)^{-1}
\int_{\{X=x,\ A\in B\}} Y\,dP^{\mathrm F}
=
\int_B m_x^{\mathrm F}(a)\pi_x(a)\,da.
\]
Moreover, for every \(x\in\mathcal X\) and every \(a\in[0,\bar\delta]\),
\[
m_x^{\mathrm F}(a)=\mu_x^P(a).
\]
Consequently, for every \(\delta\in[0,\bar\delta]\), the following identities hold:
\[
d_\delta(a)\in \operatorname{supp}\{\pi_x(a)\,da\text{ on }[0,1]\}
\quad
\text{for each }x\in\mathcal X\text{ and for conditional-treatment-a.e. }a,
\]
\[
Y(d_\delta(A))
=
Y\mathbf 1\{\delta<A\}+Y(\delta)\mathbf 1\{A\leq\delta\}
\quad P^{\mathrm F}\text{-a.s.},
\]
and, with
\[
\psi_\delta(P^{\mathrm F})=\int Y(d_\delta(A))\,dP^{\mathrm F},
\qquad
\nu_\delta(P)=\int Y\mathbf 1\{\delta<A\}\,dP,
\qquad
q_x(\delta)=\int_0^\delta \pi_x(a)\,da,
\]
the causal clamp mean equals the observed clamp target
\[
\psi_\delta(P^{\mathrm F})
=
\nu_\delta(P)+\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p_xq_x(\delta)\mu_x^P(\delta)
=
\theta_\delta(P).
\]
\end{propositionv}

\begin{propositionv}{prop:observed-margin-surjectivity}[Observed margin surjectivity]*
Fix \(J\in\mathbb N\) and constants \(\beta,\kappa,L,c_-,c_+,p_{\min},\bar\delta,\alpha\in\mathbb R\). Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Regime constants.)} \(0<J\), \(0<\beta\), \(0\leq \kappa\), \(0<L\), \(0<c_-\), \(c_-\leq \kappa+1\), \(\kappa+1\leq c_+\), \(0<p_{\min}\), \(p_{\min}\leq 1/J\), \(0<\bar\delta<1\), and \(0<\alpha<1/2\).
\item \textbf{(Observed model.)} \(P\in\mathcal M\) means that \(P\) satisfies \cref{obj:def:model-class} with constants \((\beta,\kappa,L,c_-,c_+,p_{\min})\).
\item \textbf{(Full-data model.)} \(P^{\mathrm F}\in\mathcal M^{\mathrm F}\) means that \(P^{\mathrm F}\) satisfies \cref{obj:def:full-data-model-class} with constants \((\beta,\kappa,L,c_-,c_+,p_{\min},\bar\delta)\).
\end{itemize}
Then, for every \(P\in\mathcal M\), there exists \(P^{\mathrm F}\in\mathcal M^{\mathrm F}\) whose observed \((X,A,Y)\)-margin is exactly \(P\). Hence the observed-margin map from \(\mathcal M^{\mathrm F}\) onto \(\mathcal M\) is surjective.

Moreover, for every \(n\in\mathbb N\) and every \(\delta\in[0,\bar\delta]\), the causal frontier criteria in \cref{obj:def:causal-frontier-criteria} satisfy
\[
R_{n,\mathrm F}^{\star}(\delta)=R_n^\star(\delta)
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
L_{n,\mathrm F}^{\star}(\delta,\alpha)=L_n^\star(\delta,\alpha).
\]
Here \(R_n^\star(\delta)\) is the infimum, over observed-measurable estimators with values in \([0,1]\), of the worst-case absolute-error risk over \(P\in\mathcal M\) for the observed clamp target at threshold \(\delta\), and \(L_n^\star(\delta,\alpha)\) is the infimum, over uniformly honest observed-measurable confidence procedures at level \(1-\alpha\), of the worst-case expected interval length over \(P\in\mathcal M\).
\end{propositionv}
% CAUSALSMITH-CITED-SCOPE-BEGIN prop:observed-margin-surjectivity

The cited source proof is not formalized here: Lean verifies its use and all remaining steps. If that cited conclusion is false, the portions of this result that depend on it are not certified.}

\begin{definitionv}{synth_11}[Real-to-extended embedding]
Under the notation and hypotheses of the objects introduced earlier in the paper, a real number \(t\in\mathbb R\) is embedded into the extended nonnegative reals by
\[
t\longmapsto \max\{t,0\}\in[0,\infty]\;.
\]
The image is finite and equals the positive part of \(t\), so real expected-length bounds are compared with extended-real expected lengths through this embedding.
\end{definitionv}

\begin{theoremv}{thm:causal-frontier-lift}[Causal frontier lift]
Let \(J\in\mathbb N\), and let \(\beta,\kappa,L,c_-,c_+,p_{\min},\bar\delta,\alpha\in\mathbb R\). Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Regime constants.)} The constants satisfy
\[
0<J,\qquad
\beta>0,\qquad
\kappa\geq0,\qquad
L>0,\qquad
c_->0,\qquad
c_-\leq \kappa+1\leq c_+,
\]
\[
p_{\min}>0,\qquad
p_{\min}\leq \frac1J,\qquad
0<\bar\delta<1,\qquad
0<\alpha<\frac12 .
\]
\item \textbf{(Threshold sequence.)} The deterministic thresholds \((\delta_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}\) satisfy
\[
0\leq \delta_n\leq \bar\delta
\]
for every \(n\in\mathbb N\).
\item \textbf{(Split blocks.)} For each \(n\in\mathbb N\), \(B_n=(I_{0,n},I_{1,n},I_{2,n})\) is a deterministic three-way split with pairwise disjoint blocks and
\[
\left\lfloor \frac n4\right\rfloor\leq |I_{0,n}|,\qquad
\left\lfloor \frac n4\right\rfloor\leq |I_{1,n}|,\qquad
\left\lfloor \frac n4\right\rfloor\leq |I_{2,n}|.
\]
\end{itemize}
Let \(h_n\), the information-balance bandwidth for \(\delta_n\), be as in \cref{obj:def:bandwidth}, and let
\[
r_n=n^{-1/2}+\delta_n^{\kappa+1}h_n^\beta
\]
be the frontier rate from \cref{obj:def:frontier}. Then there exist constants \(c,C\in\mathbb R\), with \(0<c<C\), depending only on these regime constants, such that, for every threshold sequence and every deterministic split-block sequence satisfying the preceding conditions, all sufficiently large \(n\) satisfy the following conclusions.

The total-Gram estimator \(\widehat\theta_n\) in \cref{obj:def:total-gram-estimator}, formed with split \(B_n\), order \(\ell=\lceil\beta\rceil-1\), bandwidth \(h_n\), and threshold \(\delta_n\), is observed-sample measurable. The corresponding bias-aware interval \(\mathrm{CI}_n\) in \cref{obj:def:honest-interval}, formed with the same split, order, bandwidth, and threshold, is an observed-sample measurable interval.

For the causal minimax criteria \(R_{n,\mathrm F}^\star\) and \(L_{n,\mathrm F}^\star\) in \cref{obj:def:causal-frontier-criteria},
\[
c r_n\leq R_{n,\mathrm F}^\star
\leq
\sup_{P^{\mathrm F}\in\mathcal M^{\mathrm F}}
\mathbb E_{(P^{\mathrm F})^{\otimes n}}
\left|\widehat\theta_n-\psi_{\delta_n}(P^{\mathrm F})\right|
\leq C r_n,
\]
\[
\inf_{P^{\mathrm F}\in\mathcal M^{\mathrm F}}
(P^{\mathrm F})^{\otimes n}\{\psi_{\delta_n}(P^{\mathrm F})\in \mathrm{CI}_n\}
\geq 1-\alpha,
\]
\[
\sup_{P^{\mathrm F}\in\mathcal M^{\mathrm F}}
\mathbb E_{(P^{\mathrm F})^{\otimes n}}\operatorname{len}(\mathrm{CI}_n)
\leq C r_n.
\]
Moreover, in the extended nonnegative-real order, after embedding the nonnegative real bounds into \(\mathbb R_{\geq0}\cup\{\infty\}\),
\[
c r_n\leq L_{n,\mathrm F}^\star\leq C r_n .
\]
\end{theoremv}

\begin{definitionv}{def:continuity-model-class}[Continuity-only model class \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}\)]
\(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}\) is the set of laws
\[
P\in\mathcal P(\mathcal X\times[0,1]\times[0,1])
\]
satisfying \cref{obj:ass:conditional-density-law,obj:ass:stratum-mass,obj:ass:polynomial-thinning} and the following continuity condition: for every \(x\in\mathcal X\), an almost-everywhere version of
\[
a\mapsto \mathbb E_P[Y\mid A=a,X=x]
\]
admits a continuous extension to \([0,\bar\delta]\). The continuity extension is required memberwise for each stratum.
\end{definitionv}

\begin{definitionv}{def:continuity-clamp-functional}[Continuity clamp target \(\theta_{\delta,\mathrm{cont}}(P)\)]
For \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}\) and \(0\leq\delta\leq\bar\delta\), with \(q_x(\delta)\) as in \cref{obj:def:clamp-functional} and \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}\) as in \cref{obj:def:continuity-model-class}, define
\[
 \theta_{\delta,\mathrm{cont}}(P)
 =
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[Y\mathbf 1\{A>\delta\}\right]
 +
 \sum_{x\in\mathcal X}
 p_xq_x(\delta)\mu_{x,\mathrm{cont}}^P(\delta).
\]
\end{definitionv}

\begin{definitionv}{def:continuity-frontier}[Continuity frontier \(s_n\)]
Define the continuity-only frontier rate by
\[
s_n=n^{-1/2}+\delta_n^{\kappa+1}.
\]
\end{definitionv}

\begin{algorithmv}{def:continuity-fallback-estimator}[Continuity fallback estimator \(\widehat\theta_{n,\mathrm{cont}}\)]
The inputs are the deterministic split blocks \(I_0,I_1\), the threshold \(\delta_n\), and the observations \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\).
\begin{enumerate}
\item Define the retained-course empirical mean
\[
\widehat\nu_n
=
|I_0|^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_0}Y_i\mathbf 1\{A_i>\delta_n\}.
\]
\item For each \(x\in\mathcal X\), define the empirical lower-threshold atom mass
\[
\widehat b_x
=
|I_1|^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_1}\mathbf 1\{X_i=x,A_i\leq\delta_n\}.
\]
\item Output the fixed-regression-fallback estimator
\[
\widehat\theta_{n,\mathrm{cont}}
=
\Pi_{[0,1]}\left\{\widehat\nu_n+\frac12\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}\widehat b_x\right\}.
\]
\end{enumerate}
\end{algorithmv}

\begin{algorithmv}{def:continuity-honest-interval}[Continuity honest interval \(\mathrm{CI}_{n,\mathrm{cont}}\)]
The inputs are the split blocks \(I_0,I_1\), the level \(\alpha\), the estimator \(\widehat\theta_{n,\mathrm{cont}}\), and the empirical masses \(\widehat b_x\).
\begin{enumerate}
\item For \(j=0,1\), define the split-specific Hoeffding radius
\[
t_{j,\alpha}
=
\sqrt{\frac{\log(4/\alpha)}{2|I_j|}}.
\]
\item Define the empirical total lower-threshold atom mass
\[
\widehat B_n
=
\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}\widehat b_x.
\]
\item Output the Hoeffding interval
\[
\mathrm{CI}_{n,\mathrm{cont}}
=
\left[
\widehat\theta_{n,\mathrm{cont}}-t_{0,\alpha}-t_{1,\alpha}-\frac12\widehat B_n,\,
\widehat\theta_{n,\mathrm{cont}}+t_{0,\alpha}+t_{1,\alpha}+\frac12\widehat B_n
\right]\cap[0,1].
\]
\end{enumerate}
\end{algorithmv}

\begin{definitionv}{def:continuity-full-data-model-class}[Continuity full-data class \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}^{\mathrm F}\)]
Define \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}^{\mathrm F}\) as the collection of full-data law packages \(P^{\mathrm F}\) with a memberwise standard Borel latent-response space \(\mathcal U\), latent variable \(U\), jointly Borel stratum-specific response maps \(g_x\), and jointly measurable potential-outcome process \(\{Y(a):a\in[0,1]\}\), such that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Observed margin.)} The observed \((X,A,Y)\)-margin of \(P^{\mathrm F}\) belongs to \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}\) in \cref{obj:def:continuity-model-class}.
\item \textbf{(Consistency.)} The package satisfies \cref{obj:ass:consistency}.
\item \textbf{(Exchangeability.)} The package satisfies \cref{obj:ass:exchangeability}.
\item \textbf{(Response continuity.)} The package satisfies \cref{obj:ass:full-data-response-continuity}.
\end{itemize}
The carrier spaces \(\mathcal U\) may vary with \(P^{\mathrm F}\).
\end{definitionv}

\begin{definitionv}{def:continuity-frontier-criteria}[Continuity frontier criteria \(R_{n,\mathrm{cont}}^\star\) and \(L_{n,\mathrm{cont}}^\star\)]
For estimators and intervals measurable with respect to \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\), define the continuity-only observed minimax absolute-error risk by
\[
R_{n,\mathrm{cont}}^\star
=
\inf_{\widehat\theta}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}}
\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}
\left|\widehat\theta-\theta_{\delta_n,\mathrm{cont}}(P)\right|.
\]
Define the continuity-only observed minimax honest expected length by
\[
L_{n,\mathrm{cont}}^\star
=
\inf_{C_n:\,\inf_{P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}}P^{\otimes n}
\{\theta_{\delta_n,\mathrm{cont}}(P)\in C_n\}\geq1-\alpha}
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}}
\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}\!\left[\operatorname{len}(C_n)\right].
\]
For the full-data continuity-only class, define the causal minimax absolute-error risk by
\[
R_{n,\mathrm{cont},\mathrm F}^\star
=
\inf_{\widehat\psi}\sup_{P^{\mathrm F}\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}^{\mathrm F}}
\mathbb E_{(P^{\mathrm F})^{\otimes n}}
\left|\widehat\psi-\psi_{\delta_n}(P^{\mathrm F})\right|.
\]
Define the continuity-only causal minimax honest expected length by
\[
L_{n,\mathrm{cont},\mathrm F}^\star
=
\inf_{C_n:\,\inf_{P^{\mathrm F}\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}^{\mathrm F}}
(P^{\mathrm F})^{\otimes n}\{\psi_{\delta_n}(P^{\mathrm F})\in C_n\}\geq1-\alpha}
\sup_{P^{\mathrm F}\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}^{\mathrm F}}
\mathbb E_{(P^{\mathrm F})^{\otimes n}}\!\left[\operatorname{len}(C_n)\right].
\]
\end{definitionv}

\begin{propositionv}{prop:continuity-causal-bridge}[Continuity causal bridge]
Let \(J\in\mathbb N\), let \(\kappa,c_-,c_+,p_{\min},\bar\delta\in\mathbb R\), and let \(P^{\mathrm F}\) be a full-data law package with observed margin \(P\).  Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Full-data continuity model.)} \(P^{\mathrm F}\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}^{\mathrm F}\) with constants \((\kappa,c_-,c_+,p_{\min},\bar\delta)\), as in \cref{obj:def:continuity-full-data-model-class}.
\item \textbf{(Design constants.)} \(J>0\), \(\kappa\geq0\), \(c_->0\), \(c_-\leq \kappa+1\leq c_+\), \(0<p_{\min}\leq 1/J\), and \(0<\bar\delta<1\).
\end{itemize}
For each \(x\in\mathcal X\) and \(a\in\mathbb R\), define the full-data response mean by
\[
m_x^{\mathrm F}(a)
=
P^{\mathrm F}(X=x)^{-1}
\int_{\{X=x\}} g_x(a,U)\,dP^{\mathrm F}.
\]
Then, for every \(x\in\mathcal X\) and every \(a\in[0,\bar\delta]\),
\[
m_x^{\mathrm F}(a)=\mu_{x,\mathrm{cont}}^P(a).
\]
Moreover, if
\[
\psi_\delta(P^{\mathrm F})
=
\int Y\!\left(d_\delta(A)\right)\,dP^{\mathrm F},
\]
then, for every \(\delta\in[0,\bar\delta]\),
\[
\psi_\delta(P^{\mathrm F})
=
\theta_{\delta,\mathrm{cont}}(P),
\]
where \(\theta_{\delta,\mathrm{cont}}(P)\) is the continuity-only clamp functional in \cref{obj:def:continuity-clamp-functional}.
\end{propositionv}

\begin{propositionv}{prop:continuity-observed-margin-surjectivity}[Observed-margin surjectivity]*
Let \(J\in\mathbb N\) and let \(\kappa,c_-,c_+,p_{\min},\bar\delta,\alpha\in\mathbb R\). Suppose that the continuity-regime design constants used in \cref{obj:def:continuity-model-class,obj:def:continuity-full-data-model-class,obj:def:continuity-frontier-criteria} hold for \((J,\kappa,c_-,c_+,p_{\min},\bar\delta)\), and that \(0<\alpha<1/2\).

Then the observed-margin map from \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}^{\mathrm F}\) onto \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}\) is surjective: for every \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}\), there exists \(P^{\mathrm F}\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}^{\mathrm F}\) whose observed margin is \(P\). Moreover, for every \(n\in\mathbb N\) and every \(\delta\in[0,\bar\delta]\), the four continuity-frontier criteria of \cref{obj:def:continuity-frontier-criteria}, evaluated at \((J,n,\kappa,c_-,c_+,p_{\min},\bar\delta,\delta,\alpha)\), satisfy
\[
R_{n,\mathrm{cont},\mathrm F}^\star
=
R_{n,\mathrm{cont}}^\star,
\qquad
L_{n,\mathrm{cont},\mathrm F}^\star
=
L_{n,\mathrm{cont}}^\star .
\]
\end{propositionv}
% CAUSALSMITH-CITED-SCOPE-BEGIN prop:continuity-observed-margin-surjectivity
\verificationfootnotetext{\textbf{Formalization scope.} This result uses the published conclusion \citep{Kallenberg2002Foundations} (Theorem 6.3 (conditional distribution)). The cited source proof is not formalized here: Lean verifies its use and all remaining steps. If that cited conclusion is false, the portions of this result that depend on it are not certified.}
% CAUSALSMITH-CITED-SCOPE-END prop:continuity-observed-margin-surjectivity

\begin{definitionv}{synth_13}[Observed margin of a full-data law]
For a full-data law package $P^{\mathrm F}$ governing $(X,A,Y,U,\{Y(a):a\in[0,1]\})$, define $P^{\mathrm F}_{\mathrm{obs}}$ to be the observed-data marginal law of $(X,A,Y)$. Equivalently, if $\pi_{\mathrm{obs}}(X,A,Y,U,\{Y(a)\})=(X,A,Y)$ is the coordinate projection onto $\mathcal X\times[0,1]\times[0,1]$, then $P^{\mathrm F}_{\mathrm{obs}}=(\pi_{\mathrm{obs}})_{\#}P^{\mathrm F}$.
\end{definitionv}

\begin{theoremv}{thm:continuity-only-frontier}[Continuity frontier characterization]*
Fix \(J\in\mathbb N\) and constants \(\kappa,c_-,c_+,p_{\min},\bar\delta,\alpha\in\mathbb R\). Suppose
\[
0<J,
\qquad
0\leq \kappa,
\qquad
0<c_-,
\qquad
c_-\leq \kappa+1\leq c_+,
\qquad
0<p_{\min}\leq \frac{1}{J},
\qquad
0<\bar\delta<1,
\qquad
0<\alpha<\frac12.
\]
Then there exist constants \(c,C\in\mathbb R\) with \(0<c<C\) such that the following statements hold.

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Uniform frontier bounds.)} For every deterministic threshold sequence \((\delta_n)_{n\geq1}\) with \(\delta_n\in[0,\bar\delta]\) for all \(n\), and for every deterministic sequence \(B_{\bullet}=(B_n)_{n\geq1}\) of admissible three-way split blocks, all sufficiently large \(n\) satisfy the following bounds. With
\[
s_n=n^{-1/2}+\delta_n^{\kappa+1},
\]
and with \(R_{n,\mathrm{cont}}^\star\), \(L_{n,\mathrm{cont}}^\star\), \(R_{n,\mathrm{cont},\mathrm F}^\star\), and \(L_{n,\mathrm{cont},\mathrm F}^\star\) as in \cref{obj:def:continuity-frontier-criteria},
\[
c s_n\leq R_{n,\mathrm{cont}}^\star
\leq
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}}
\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}
\left|\widehat\theta_{n,\mathrm{cont}}-\theta_{\delta_n,\mathrm{cont}}(P)\right|
\leq C s_n,
\]
the interval \(\mathrm{CI}_{n,\mathrm{cont}}\) has uniform coverage at least \(1-\alpha\) over \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}\), its worst-case expected length is at most \(C s_n\), and
\[
c s_n\leq L_{n,\mathrm{cont}}^\star.
\]
Moreover,
\[
R_{n,\mathrm{cont},\mathrm F}^\star=R_{n,\mathrm{cont}}^\star,
\qquad
L_{n,\mathrm{cont},\mathrm F}^\star=L_{n,\mathrm{cont}}^\star,
\]
and the same estimator and interval satisfy
\[
R_{n,\mathrm{cont},\mathrm F}^\star
\leq
\sup_{P^{\mathrm F}\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}^{\mathrm F}}
\mathbb E_{(P^{\mathrm F}_{\mathrm{obs}})^{\otimes n}}
\left|\widehat\theta_{n,\mathrm{cont}}-\psi_{\delta_n}(P^{\mathrm F})\right|
\leq C s_n,
\]
with causal coverage at least \(1-\alpha\) uniformly over \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}^{\mathrm F}\) and causal worst-case expected length at most \(C s_n\).

\item \textbf{(Elbow and null-threshold rates.)} For the continuity-only rate in \cref{obj:def:continuity-frontier},
\[
s_n\bigl(\delta_n=n^{-1/(2(\kappa+1))}\bigr)
\asymp n^{-1/2},
\qquad
s_n(0)\asymp n^{-1/2}.
\]

\item \textbf{(Fixed positive thresholds.)} For every deterministic threshold sequence \((\delta_n)_{n\geq1}\) with \(\delta_n\in[0,\bar\delta]\) for all \(n\), every \(\delta_0\in(0,\bar\delta]\), and \(\delta_n\to\delta_0\),
\[
R_{n,\mathrm{cont}}^\star \not\to 0,
\qquad
L_{n,\mathrm{cont}}^\star \not\to 0.
\]
\end{itemize}
\end{theoremv}
% CAUSALSMITH-CITED-SCOPE-BEGIN thm:continuity-only-frontier
\verificationfootnotetext{\textbf{Formalization scope.} This result uses the published conclusion \citep{Hoeffding1963} (Theorem 2, specialized to unit ranges and two tails). The cited source proof is not formalized here: Lean verifies its use and all remaining steps. If that cited conclusion is false, the portions of this result that depend on it are not certified.}
% CAUSALSMITH-CITED-SCOPE-END thm:continuity-only-frontier

\begin{definitionv}{def:exact-modulus-handle}[Exact modulus radius]
With notation as in \cref{obj:def:local-design-notation,obj:def:model-class}, fix \(P\in\mathcal M\) under the displayed \(\beta,\kappa,L,c_-,c_+,p_{\min}\) member conditions, a deterministic split \(B=(I_0,I_1,I_2)\) with pairwise-disjoint blocks satisfying \(|I_m|\geq \lfloor n/4\rfloor\) for \(m=0,1,2\), a stratum \(x\in\mathcal X\), a local-polynomial degree \(\ell\in\mathbb N\), a threshold \(\delta\), a bandwidth \(h>0\), and a multiplier \(t\geq0\). For a realized observed sample \(z=(O_1,\ldots,O_n)\), with \(O_i=(X_i,A_i,Y_i)\), set
\[
u_i=\frac{A_i-\delta}{h},
\qquad
S_{z,x}=\{i\in I_2:X_i=x,\ 0\leq u_i\leq1\}.
\]
The affine weight set is
\[
\mathcal W_{z,x}
=
\left\{
w=(w_i)_{i=1}^n\in\mathbb R^n:
w_i=0\ \text{whenever } i\notin I_2\ \text{or }X_i\neq x\ \text{or }u_i\notin[0,1],
\quad
\sum_{i\in I_2}w_i u_i^j=\mathbf 1\{j=0\}\ \text{for }j=0,\ldots,\ell
\right\}.
\]
For \(w\in\mathcal W_{z,x}\), let \(B^{\mathrm H}_{z,x}(w)\) denote the exact Hölder bias term from the \((\beta,L)\)-Hölder regression class in \cref{obj:ass:holder-regression}. Define the realized affine-modulus radius by
\[
R^{\mathrm{ex}}_{z,x}(t)
=
\inf\left\{
B^{\mathrm H}_{z,x}(w)
+
t\left(\sum_{i\in I_2}w_i^2\right)^{1/2}
:
w\in\mathcal W_{z,x}
\right\},
\]
with the real-valued convention that this infimum is \(0\) when the displayed feasible set is empty. The integrated exact-modulus radius is
\[
M^{\mathrm{ex}}_{x}(P,B,\ell,\beta,\kappa,L,c_-,c_+,p_{\min},\delta,h,t)
=
\int R^{\mathrm{ex}}_{z,x}(t)\,\mathrm dP^{\otimes n}(z),
\]
where \(P^{\otimes n}\) is the canonical product law of the observed sample. Both \(R^{\mathrm{ex}}_{z,x}(t)\) and \(M^{\mathrm{ex}}_{x}(P,B,\ell,\beta,\kappa,L,c_-,c_+,p_{\min},\delta,h,t)\) are radius, or half-length, quantities.
\end{definitionv}

\begin{definitionv}{synth_21}[Exact-modulus radius \(W_{n,B_n}\)]
Adopt the notation and hypotheses of the objects introduced earlier in the paper.  Fix \(P\in\mathcal M\), a deterministic third split block \(I_2\), a stratum \(x\in\mathcal X\), and a multiplier \(t\geq0\).  For a realized design \(z=\{(X_i,A_i):i\in I_2\}\), set
\[
u_i=\frac{A_i-\delta_n}{h_n},
\qquad
S_{z,x}=\{i\in I_2:X_i=x,\ 0\leq u_i\leq1\}.
\]
Let
\[
\mathcal W_{z,x}
=
\left\{
w=(w_i)_{i\in I_2}\in\mathbb R^{I_2}:
w_i=0\ \text{for }i\notin S_{z,x},\
\sum_{i\in I_2}w_i u_i^j=\mathbf 1\{j=0\}\ \text{for }j=0,\ldots,\ell
\right\}.
\]
Let \(\mathcal H_{\beta,L}\) be the class of continuous functions \(f:[0,1]\to[0,1]\) satisfying the declared order-\(\ell\) Hölder Taylor-remainder bound with exponent \(\beta\) and radius \(L\).  For \(w\in\mathcal W_{z,x}\), define the realized Hölder bias functional
\[
B_{z,x}(w)
=
\sup_{f\in\mathcal H_{\beta,L}}
\left|
\sum_{i\in I_2}w_i f(A_i)-f(\delta_n)
\right|.
\]
The realized affine-modulus radius at multiplier \(t\) is
\[
\mathcal R_{z,x}(t)
=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle
\inf_{w\in\mathcal W_{z,x}}
\left\{
B_{z,x}(w)
+
t\left(\sum_{i\in I_2}w_i^2\right)^{1/2}
\right\},
&\mathcal W_{z,x}\neq\varnothing,\\[1ex]
0,&\mathcal W_{z,x}=\varnothing.
\end{cases}
\]
The integrated exact-modulus radius is
\[
\mathfrak R_{n,x}(P,I_2;t)
=
\int
\mathcal R_{z,x}(t)\,
\mathrm d(P_{X,A}^{\otimes I_2})(z),
\]
where \(P_{X,A}^{\otimes I_2}\) is the independent observed-design product law on the coordinates in \(I_2\).

If \(B_n=(I_{0,n},I_{1,n},I_{2,n})\) is an admissible deterministic three-way split at sample size \(n\), its worst integrated exact-modulus radius is
\[
W_{n,B_n}
=
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M}\sup_{x\in\mathcal X}
\mathfrak R_{n,x}\!\left(P,I_{2,n};t_\alpha\right),
\qquad
t_\alpha=\sqrt{\log(12J/\alpha)/2}.
\]
Thus \(W_{n,B_n}\) is a radius quantity computed from the third block of \(B_n\), and the associated untruncated symmetric full length is \(2W_{n,B_n}\).
\end{definitionv}

\begin{definitionv}{synth_20}[Exact-modulus interval]
Assume the notation, model conditions, and preceding constructions in the objects introduced earlier in the paper. Fix an admissible deterministic three-way split \(B_n=(I_0,I_1,I_2)\) at sample size \(n\). For a realized observed sample \(z\), let \(\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{TG}}_{n,B_n}(z)\) be the total-Gram estimator formed with the blocks in \(B_n\), and evaluate the realized affine-modulus radius \(R^{\mathrm{ex}}_{z,x}(t_\alpha)\) on the \((X,A)\)-projection of \(z\) using the third block \(I_2\), where
\[
t_\alpha=\sqrt{\log(12J/\alpha)/2}.
\]
Define
\[
R_{n,B_n}(z)
=
\sup_{x\in\mathcal X}
R^{\mathrm{ex}}_{z,x}(t_\alpha).
\]
The exact-modulus interval is
\[
C^{\mathrm{mod}}_{n,B_n}(z)
=
\left[
\max\left\{0,\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{TG}}_{n,B_n}(z)-R_{n,B_n}(z)\right\},
\min\left\{1,\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{TG}}_{n,B_n}(z)+R_{n,B_n}(z)\right\}
\right].
\]
Its worst-case expected length over the observed-data model is
\[
\ell^{\mathrm{mod}}_{n,B_n}
=
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M}
\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}
\left[
\operatorname{len}\!\left(C^{\mathrm{mod}}_{n,B_n}\right)
\right].
\]
\end{definitionv}

\begin{remarkv}{oeq:sharp-constant}[Sharp length calibration]
The sharp constant question asks for the following property. For every
\[
 J\in\mathbb N,\qquad
 \beta,\kappa,L,c_-,c_+,p_{\min},\bar\delta,\alpha\in\mathbb R
\]
satisfying
\[
 J>0,\quad \beta>0,\quad \kappa\geq0,\quad L>0,\quad c_->0,\quad
 c_-\leq \kappa+1\leq c_+,\quad
 0<p_{\min}\leq \frac1J,\quad
 0<\bar\delta<1,\quad 0<\alpha<\frac12,
\]
there is a constant \(c>0\) such that every deterministic threshold sequence
\(\delta_{\bullet}=(\delta_n)_{n\geq1}\) with \(0\leq\delta_n\leq\bar\delta\) for all \(n\), and whose phase-boundary ratio satisfies either
\[
 \frac{\delta_n}{\delta_{\mathrm{crit},n}}\longrightarrow q
 \quad\text{for some }q\geq0
\]
or
\[
 \frac{\delta_n}{\delta_{\mathrm{crit},n}}\longrightarrow\infty,
\]
has the following simultaneous calibration properties. First,
\[
 \frac{L_n^\star}{r_n}\longrightarrow c,
 \qquad
 r_n=n^{-1/2}+\delta_n^{\kappa+1}h_n^\beta,
\]
where \(h_n\) is the information-balance bandwidth from \cref{obj:def:bandwidth} and \(r_n\) is the frontier from \cref{obj:def:frontier}. Second, there exists a deterministic sequence
\(B_{\bullet}=(B_n)_{n\geq1}\) of admissible three-way split blocks such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal M}
 P^{\otimes n}
 \left\{
   \theta_{\delta_n}(P)\in C^{\mathrm{mod}}_{n,B_n}
 \right\}
 \geq 1-\alpha,
\]
where \(C^{\mathrm{mod}}_{n,B_n}\) is the exact-modulus interval obtained from the split \(B_n\) using the exact-modulus construction of \cref{obj:def:exact-modulus-handle}. Its worst-case expected length satisfies
\[
 \frac{\ell^{\mathrm{mod}}_{n,B_n}}{r_n}\longrightarrow c.
\]
Finally, the same sequence \(B_{\bullet}\) admits least-favorable mixed-experiment witnesses: there are a constant \(D>0\), an amplitude \(0<\mathsf{amplitude}\leq1/4\), and sequences
\[
 P_0,P_{\mathrm{reg}},P_{\mathrm{loc}}:\mathbb N\to\mathcal M
\]
such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\), the three laws satisfy the clamp-model member conditions; their \(n\)-sample laws are the product laws in \cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling}; the pair \((P_0(n),P_{\mathrm{reg}}(n))\) has the declared global Bernoulli shift at scale \(n^{-1/2}\); the pair \((P_0(n),P_{\mathrm{loc}}(n))\) has the declared localized Bernoulli perturbation at \(\beta\), \(\delta_n\), \(h_n\), and \(\mathsf{amplitude}\); and
\[
 \chi^2\!\left(P_{\mathrm{reg}}(n)^{\otimes n}\middle\Vert P_0(n)^{\otimes n}\right)\leq D,
 \qquad
 \chi^2\!\left(P_{\mathrm{loc}}(n)^{\otimes n}\middle\Vert P_0(n)^{\otimes n}\right)\leq D.
\]
With
\[
 \Delta_n^{\mathrm{mix}}
 =
 \left|\theta_{\delta_n}\!\left(P_{\mathrm{reg}}(n)\right)-
          \theta_{\delta_n}\!\left(P_0(n)\right)\right|
  +
 \left|\theta_{\delta_n}\!\left(P_{\mathrm{loc}}(n)\right)-
          \theta_{\delta_n}\!\left(P_0(n)\right)\right|,
\]
and with \(W_{n,B_n}\) denoting the worst integrated exact-modulus radius from
\cref{obj:def:exact-modulus-handle} computed using the third block in \(B_n\), the matching limits are
\[
 \frac{\Delta_n^{\mathrm{mix}}}{2W_{n,B_n}}\longrightarrow1,
 \qquad
 \frac{\ell^{\mathrm{mod}}_{n,B_n}}{2W_{n,B_n}}\longrightarrow1,
 \qquad
 \frac{2W_{n,B_n}}{L_n^\star}\longrightarrow1.
\]
\end{remarkv}

\begin{propositionv}{prop:pushforward-setup}[Clamp pushforward decomposition]
Let \(J\) be a positive integer, let \(P\in\mathcal M\) satisfy \cref{obj:def:model-class}, and let \(d_\delta(a)=\max\{a,\delta\}\) as in \cref{obj:def:clamp-policy}. Suppose the constants satisfy:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Smoothness and thinning.)} \(\beta>0\), \(\kappa\geq 0\), \(L>0\), and \(0<c_-\leq \kappa+1\leq c_+\).
\item \textbf{(Stratum mass.)} \(0<p_{\min}\leq 1/J\).
\item \textbf{(Threshold and level.)} \(0<\bar\delta<1\) and \(0<\alpha<1/2\).
\item \textbf{(Evaluation point.)} \(x\in\mathcal X\) and \(0\leq\delta\leq\bar\delta\).
\end{itemize}
Define the lower-tail atom mass
\[
q_x(\delta)=\int_{[0,\delta]}\pi_x(a)\,da .
\]
Then the conditional pushforward law of the clamped treatment satisfies
\[
P\{d_\delta(A)\in da\mid X=x\}
=
P\{A\in da,\ A\in(\delta,1]\mid X=x\}
+
q_x(\delta)\,\delta_\delta(da),
\]
and the atom mass obeys
\[
\frac{c_-\,\delta^{\kappa+1}}{\kappa+1}
\leq
q_x(\delta)
\leq
\frac{c_+\,\delta^{\kappa+1}}{\kappa+1}.
\]
\end{propositionv}

\begin{propositionv}{prop:policy-support}[Policy support preservation]
Let \(P\), \(\beta,\kappa,L,c_-,c_+,p_{\min},\bar\delta,\alpha\), \(x\), and \(\delta\) satisfy:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Model.)} \(P\in\mathcal M\) satisfies \cref{obj:def:model-class} with constants \(\beta,\kappa,L,c_-,c_+,p_{\min}\).
\item \textbf{(Regime constants.)} \(J\ge 1\), \(0<\beta\), \(0\le \kappa\), \(0<L\), \(0<c_-\le \kappa+1\le c_+\), \(0<p_{\min}\le 1/J\), \(0<\bar\delta<1\), and \(0<\alpha<1/2\).
\item \textbf{(Stratum and threshold.)} \(x\in\mathcal X\) and \(0\le \delta\le \bar\delta\).
\end{itemize}
Then, for conditional-treatment almost every \(a\) in stratum \(x\), the clamped value \(d_\delta(a)=\max\{a,\delta\}\) from \cref{obj:def:clamp-policy} is a support point of the conditional natural-treatment law given \(X=x\): every open neighborhood \(U\) of \(d_\delta(a)\) has positive conditional-treatment measure in stratum \(x\),
\[
0<\Pr_P(A\in U\mid X=x).
\]
\end{propositionv}

\begin{lemmav}{lem:shifted-moment-coercivity}[Uniform shifted coercivity]
Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Degree.)} Fix a polynomial degree \(\ell\in\mathbb N\).
\item \textbf{(Exponent.)} Fix a thinning exponent \(\kappa\in\mathbb R\).
\item \textbf{(Nonnegativity.)} The exponent satisfies \(0\le \kappa\), as in \cref{obj:ass:polynomial-thinning}.
\item \textbf{(Reference matrix.)} Let \(M_{\ell,\kappa,\rho}\) denote the normalized population reference moment matrix in \cref{obj:def:local-design-notation}.
\end{itemize}
Then there exists a constant \(c=c(\ell,\kappa)>0\) such that, for every shift \(\rho\ge 0\) and every vector \(z=(z_0,\ldots,z_\ell)\in\mathbb R^{\ell+1}\),
\[
c\sum_{j=0}^{\ell} z_j^2
\le
z^\top M_{\ell,\kappa,\rho}z .
\]
\end{lemmav}

\begin{lemmav}{lem:lambda-star-positive}[Positive Gram constant]
In the local-design notation of \cref{obj:def:local-design-notation}, suppose:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Degree.)} The polynomial degree is \(\ell\in\mathbb N\).
\item \textbf{(Thinning exponent.)} The exponent satisfies \(\kappa\ge 0\), as in \cref{obj:ass:polynomial-thinning}.
\item \textbf{(Envelope constants.)} The envelope constants satisfy \(c_->0\) and \(c_+>0\).
\end{itemize}
Then the uniform population Gram lower-bound constant
\[
\lambda_\star(\ell,\kappa,c_-,c_+)
=
\frac{c_-}{c_+}\inf_{\rho\ge 0}\lambda_{\min}(M_{\ell,\kappa,\rho})
\]
is strictly positive:
\[
\lambda_\star(\ell,\kappa,c_-,c_+)>0.
\]
\end{lemmav}

\begin{lemmav}{lem:power-window-integral-lower}[Power window integral lower bound]
Using the thinning-exponent notation of \cref{obj:ass:polynomial-thinning}, let \(\delta\) be a threshold, \(h\) a window width, and \(\kappa\) an exponent. Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Threshold.)} \(0\le \delta\).
\item \textbf{(Window width.)} \(0<h\).
\item \textbf{(Exponent.)} \(0\le \kappa\).
\end{itemize}
Then
\[
\frac{h}{2}\left(\frac{\delta+h}{2}\right)^{\kappa}
\le
\int_{\delta}^{\delta+h} a^{\kappa}\,da .
\]
\end{lemmav}

\begin{lemmav}{lem:local-window-mass}[Local window mass identity]
Let \(P\), an observed-data law, belong to the model class \(\mathcal M\) of \cref{obj:def:model-class}, with conditional treatment densities, stratum masses, and polynomial thinning as in \cref{obj:ass:conditional-density-law,obj:ass:stratum-mass,obj:ass:polynomial-thinning} for constants \((\beta,\kappa,L,c_-,c_+,p_{\min})\).  Fix:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Stratum.)} A stratum \(x\in\mathcal X\).
\item \textbf{(Threshold and width.)} A threshold \(\delta\in\mathbb R\) and a window width \(h\in\mathbb R\) with \(h>0\).
\item \textbf{(Window support.)} \([\delta,\delta+h]\subseteq[0,1]\).
\end{itemize}
Then the population mass of the local window in stratum \(x\) is
\[
\int \mathbf 1\{X=x,\ 0\le (A-\delta)/h\le 1\}\,dP
=
p_x\int_{\delta}^{\delta+h}\pi_x(a)\,da.
\]
\end{lemmav}

\begin{lemmav}{lem:local-gram-entry-integral}[Local Gram integral identity]
Fix a law \(P\in\mathcal M\) with declared constants \((\beta,\kappa,L,c_-,c_+,p_{\min})\), as in \cref{obj:def:model-class,obj:ass:conditional-density-law,obj:ass:stratum-mass,obj:ass:polynomial-thinning}.  Let \(\ell\in\mathbb N\), \(x\in\mathcal X\), and \(\delta,h\in\mathbb R\).  Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Constant signs.)} \(\kappa\ge 0\), \(c_+\ge 0\), and \(p_{\min}>0\).
\item \textbf{(Window.)} \(h>0\) and \([\delta,\delta+h]\subseteq[0,1]\).
\item \textbf{(Entries.)} \(j,k\in\{0,\ldots,\ell\}\).
\end{itemize}
For \(u_\delta(a)=(a-\delta)/h\), write \(v_\ell(u)=(1,u,\ldots,u^\ell)\) as in \cref{obj:def:local-design-notation}, and define
\[
\phi_j(O)=\mathbf 1\{0\le u_\delta(A)\le 1\}\,v_\ell(u_\delta(A))_j .
\]
Then
\[
\int \mathbf 1\{X=x,\ 0\le u_\delta(A)\le 1\}\,\phi_j(O)\phi_k(O)\,dP(O)
=
p_x\int_{\delta}^{\delta+h}
\pi_x(a)\,
v_\ell(u_\delta(a))_j\,
v_\ell(u_\delta(a))_k\,da .
\]
\end{lemmav}

\begin{lemmav}{lem:scaled-window-coercivity}[Scaled window coercivity]
Let \(\ell\in\mathbb N\), and let \(\lambda_\star=\lambda_\star(\ell,\kappa,c_-,c_+)\) be the uniform population Gram lower-bound constant from \cref{obj:def:local-design-notation}, formed with the lower and upper thinning constants in \cref{obj:ass:polynomial-thinning}. Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Shape constants.)} \(\kappa\ge 0\), \(c_->0\), and \(c_+>0\).
\item \textbf{(Window.)} \(\delta\ge 0\) and \(h>0\).
\item \textbf{(Coefficient vector.)} \(v=(v_0,\ldots,v_\ell)\in\mathbb R^{\ell+1}\).
\end{itemize}
Then
\[
\lambda_\star c_+
\left(\int_{\delta}^{\delta+h} a^\kappa\,\mathrm da\right)
\sum_{j=0}^{\ell} v_j^2
\le
c_-
\int_{\delta}^{\delta+h}
\left\{
\sum_{j=0}^{\ell}
v_j\left(\frac{a-\delta}{h}\right)^j
\right\}^2
a^\kappa\,\mathrm da .
\]
\end{lemmav}

\begin{lemmav}{lem:intercept-weight-formula}[Intercept weight formula]
Fix the local-design notation of \cref{obj:def:local-design-notation} and the split-block construction of \cref{obj:def:total-gram-estimator}.  Let \(B_n=(I_0,I_1,I_2)\) be a deterministic three-way split with pairwise disjoint blocks, each of cardinality at least \(\lfloor n/4\rfloor\).  Fix a realized sample \(z=(O_1,\ldots,O_n)\), a stratum \(x\in\mathcal X\), a degree \(\ell\), constants \(\kappa,c_-,c_+\), a threshold \(\delta\), a window width \(h\), and an index \(i\).

Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Good design.)} The good-design event \(\Omega_x\) holds for \(B_n,z,x,\ell,\kappa,c_-,c_+,\delta,h\).
\item \textbf{(Regression block.)} The index satisfies \(i\in I_2\).
\item \textbf{(Stratum match.)} The realized stratum satisfies \(X_i=x\).
\item \textbf{(Local window.)} With \(U_i=(A_i-\delta)/h\), one has \(U_i\in[0,1]\).
\end{itemize}

Then the exact local-polynomial intercept weight satisfies
\[
w_{ix}=e_0^\top G_x^{-1}v_\ell(U_i).
\]
\end{lemmav}

\begin{lemmav}{lem:good-gram-reproduction}[Good Gram reproduction]
Fix \(J,n,\ell\in\mathbb N\), a realized sample \(z=(O_1,\ldots,O_n)\), a stratum \(x\in\mathcal X\), constants \(\kappa,c_-,c_+,\delta,h\in\mathbb R\), and deterministic split blocks \(B_n=(I_0,I_1,I_2)\) as in \cref{obj:def:total-gram-estimator}.  Use the local-design notation \(U_i\), \(N_x\), \(G_x\), \(\lambda_\star\), \(\Omega_x\), and \(w_{ix}\) from \cref{obj:def:local-design-notation}.

Assume that \(\lambda_\star>0\) and that the good-design event \(\Omega_x\) holds for \(B_n,z,x,\ell,\kappa,c_-,c_+,\delta,h\).  Then the exact local-polynomial intercept weights reproduce every monomial coordinate at the threshold: for every \(j=0,\ldots,\ell\),
\[
\sum_{i\in I_2} w_{ix} U_i^j
=
\begin{cases}
1, & j=0,\\
0, & j\ne 0.
\end{cases}
\]
\end{lemmav}

\begin{lemmav}{lem:intercept-weight-pointwise}[Pointwise intercept-weight bound]
Fix integers \(J,n,\ell\), a split \(B_n=(I_0,I_1,I_2)\), a realized sample \(z=(O_1,\ldots,O_n)\), a stratum \(x\in\mathcal X\), constants \(\kappa,c_-,c_+,\delta,h\in\mathbb R\), and an index \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\).  With \(N_x\), \(\lambda_\star\), \(\Omega_x\), and \(w_{ix}\) as in \cref{obj:def:local-design-notation}, assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Split.)} The split \(B_n\) has three pairwise disjoint deterministic blocks \(I_0,I_1,I_2\), each of cardinality at least \(\lfloor n/4\rfloor\), as in \cref{obj:def:total-gram-estimator}.
\item \textbf{(Positive population Gram constant.)} \(\lambda_\star>0\).
\item \textbf{(Good design.)} The good-design event \(\Omega_x\) holds at the realized sample \(z\).
\end{itemize}
Then the exact local-polynomial intercept weight at index \(i\) satisfies
\[
|w_{ix}|
\le
\left(\frac{\lambda_\star N_x}{2}\right)^{-1}\sqrt{\ell+1}.
\]
\end{lemmav}

\begin{lemmav}{lem:bandwidth-balance}[Eventual bandwidth balance]
Let \(h_n\) denote the information-balance bandwidth from \cref{obj:def:bandwidth} formed with \(\delta_n,\beta,\kappa,\bar\delta\). Suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Hölder exponent.)} The exponent \(\beta\) appearing in \cref{obj:ass:holder-regression} satisfies \(\beta>0\).
\item \textbf{(Polynomial-thinning exponent.)} The exponent \(\kappa\) appearing in \cref{obj:ass:polynomial-thinning} satisfies \(\kappa\geq0\).
\item \textbf{(Threshold cap.)} \(0<\bar\delta<1\).
\item \textbf{(Threshold sequence.)} \((\delta_n)_{n\geq1}\) is a deterministic real sequence satisfying \(\delta_n\in[0,\bar\delta]\) for every \(n\).
\end{itemize}
Then, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
0<h_n,\qquad
h_n\leq 1-\bar\delta,\qquad
n h_n^{2\beta+1}(\delta_n+h_n)^\kappa=1.
\]
\end{lemmav}

\begin{lemmav}{lem:local-gram-coercivity}[Local Gram coercivity]
Fix an observed law \(P\in\mathcal M\) as in \cref{obj:def:model-class}, with conditional-density, stratum-mass, and polynomial-thinning components as in \cref{obj:ass:conditional-density-law,obj:ass:stratum-mass,obj:ass:polynomial-thinning}.  Fix constants \(\beta,\kappa,L,c_-,c_+\), and \(p_{\min}\), and a degree \(\ell\in\mathbb N\).  Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Design constants.)} \(\kappa\ge0\), \(c_->0\), \(c_+>0\), and \(p_{\min}>0\).
\item \textbf{(Local window.)} \(x\in\mathcal X\), \(\delta\ge0\), \(h>0\), and \(\delta+h\le1\).
\end{itemize}
For an observation \(O=(X,A,Y)\), set
\[
p_x^{\mathrm{loc}}(\delta,h)
=
\mathbb E_P\!\left[
\mathbf 1\!\left\{X=x,\ 0\le \frac{A-\delta}{h}\le 1\right\}
\right],
\]
and, for \(j=0,\ldots,\ell\), define the local monomial feature
\[
\phi_j(O)
=
\mathbf 1\!\left\{0\le \frac{A-\delta}{h}\le 1\right\}
\left(\frac{A-\delta}{h}\right)^j .
\]
Then, with \(\lambda_\star=\lambda_\star(\ell,\kappa,c_-,c_+)\) denoting the uniform population Gram lower-bound constant from \cref{obj:def:local-design-notation}, every \(v=(v_0,\ldots,v_\ell)\in\mathbb R^{\ell+1}\) satisfies
\[
\lambda_\star\,p_x^{\mathrm{loc}}(\delta,h)\sum_{j=0}^{\ell}v_j^2
\le
\sum_{j=0}^{\ell}\sum_{k=0}^{\ell}
v_jv_k\,
\mathbb E_P\!\left[
\mathbf 1\!\left\{X=x,\ 0\le \frac{A-\delta}{h}\le 1\right\}
\phi_j(O)\phi_k(O)
\right].
\]
\end{lemmav}

\begin{lemmav}{lem:good-gram-weights}[Good Gram weights]
Fix \(J,n,\ell\in\mathbb N\), a split \(B_n=(I_0,I_1,I_2)\) with pairwise disjoint blocks satisfying \(|I_r|\ge \lfloor n/4\rfloor\) for \(r=0,1,2\), an observed sample \(z=(O_1,\ldots,O_n)\), and a stratum \(x\in\mathcal X\).  Let \(\kappa,c_-,c_+,\delta,h\in\mathbb R\).  Suppose:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Positive bandwidth.)} \(h>0\).
\item \textbf{(Positive population Gram constant.)} The constant \(\lambda_\star\) from \cref{obj:def:local-design-notation} satisfies \(\lambda_\star>0\).
\item \textbf{(Good local design.)} The good-design event \(\Omega_x\) from \cref{obj:def:local-design-notation} holds for \(B_n,z,x,\ell,\kappa,c_-,c_+,\delta,h\).
\end{itemize}
Then the exact local-polynomial intercept weights \(w_{ix}\) and rescaled coordinates \(U_i\) from \cref{obj:def:local-design-notation} satisfy, for every \(j=0,\ldots,\ell\),
\[
\sum_{i\in I_2} w_{ix} U_i^j=\mathbf 1\{j=0\}.
\]
They also obey the two deterministic weight bounds
\[
\sum_{i\in I_2}|w_{ix}|
\le
\frac{2\sqrt{\ell+1}}{\lambda_\star},
\]
and, with \(N_x\) denoting the local count in \cref{obj:def:local-design-notation},
\[
\sum_{i\in I_2}w_{ix}^2
\le
\frac{4(\ell+1)}{\lambda_\star^2 N_x}.
\]
\end{lemmav}

\begin{lemmav}{lem:weight-energy-balance}[Balanced weight energy]
Let \(J,n,\ell\in\mathbb N\), let \(P\) be an observed-data law on \(J\) strata, let \(B_n=(I_0,I_1,I_2)\) be a deterministic split, and fix a stratum \(x\in\mathcal X\).  Let \(\beta,\kappa,L,c_-,c_+,p_{\min},\delta,h\in\mathbb R\), and define the observed product sampling law by
\[
P^{\otimes n}=\bigotimes_{j=1}^n P .
\]
Suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Model and sampling.)} \(P\) belongs to the observed model class \(\mathcal M\) in \cref{obj:def:model-class} with fixed constants \(\beta,\kappa,L,c_-,c_+,p_{\min}\), including the polynomial-thinning, stratum-mass, and Hölder-regression components in \cref{obj:ass:polynomial-thinning,obj:ass:stratum-mass,obj:ass:holder-regression}; the observed sample is independently drawn from \(P\) as in \cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling}; and \(B_n\) is a three-way split as in \cref{obj:def:total-gram-estimator}.
\item \textbf{(Numerical conditions.)} \(n\ge 8\), \(\beta>0\), \(\kappa\ge0\), \(c_->0\), \(c_+\ge0\), \(p_{\min}>0\), and \(\delta\ge0\).
\item \textbf{(Bandwidth and design.)} \(h>0\), \(\delta+h\le1\), and the uniform population Gram lower-bound constant \(\lambda_\star=\lambda_\star(\ell,\kappa,c_-,c_+)\) from \cref{obj:def:local-design-notation} satisfies \(\lambda_\star>0\).
\item \textbf{(Balance.)} The bandwidth is information-balanced:
\[
n h^{2\beta+1}(\delta+h)^\kappa=1.
\]
\end{itemize}
For the exact local-polynomial intercept weights \(w_{ix}\) from \cref{obj:def:local-design-notation},
\[
\int
\left(\sum_{i\in I_2} w_{ix}(z)^2\right)^{1/2}
\,dP^{\otimes n}(z)
\le
\left(
\frac{336\{4(\ell+1)/\lambda_\star^2\}}
{p_{\min}c_-/(2\cdot 2^\kappa)}
\right)^{1/2}
h^\beta .
\]
\end{lemmav}

\begin{lemmav}{lem:stabilized-interval-honesty}[Stabilized interval honesty]
Fix integers \(J\) and \(n\), deterministic split blocks \(B=(I_0,I_1,I_2)\), constants \(\beta,\kappa,L,c_-,c_+,p_{\min},\bar\delta,\alpha\), and a threshold \(\delta\).  Let \(h_n\) be the information-balance bandwidth from \cref{obj:def:bandwidth} evaluated at \((n,\delta,\beta,\kappa,\bar\delta)\), and let \(\mathrm{CI}_n\) be the stabilized interval from \cref{obj:def:honest-interval} formed with split \(B\), bandwidth \(h_n\), and threshold \(\delta\).  Suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Split blocks.)} \(B=(I_0,I_1,I_2)\) consists of three deterministic, pairwise-disjoint subsets of \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\) with
\[
|I_0|\ge \lfloor n/4\rfloor,\qquad
|I_1|\ge \lfloor n/4\rfloor,\qquad
|I_2|\ge \lfloor n/4\rfloor .
\]
\item \textbf{(Regime constants.)} The declared constants satisfy
\[
J\ge 1,\quad
\beta>0,\quad
\kappa\ge 0,\quad
L>0,\quad
0<c_-\le \kappa+1\le c_+,\quad
0<p_{\min}\le 1/J,\quad
0<\bar\delta<1,\quad
0<\alpha<1/2 .
\]
\item \textbf{(Sample size.)} \(n\ge 4\).
\item \textbf{(Threshold range.)} \(\delta\in[0,\bar\delta]\).
\item \textbf{(Interior bandwidth.)} \(0<h_n\) and \(\delta+h_n\le 1\).
\end{itemize}
Then \(\mathrm{CI}_n\) is an observed-sample measurable interval, and for every observed-data law \(P\) in the clamp model \(\mathcal M\) of \cref{obj:def:model-class},
\[
1-\alpha
\le
P^{\otimes n}\!\left\{
\theta_\delta(P)\in \mathrm{CI}_n(O_1,\ldots,O_n)
\right\},
\]
where \(\theta_\delta(P)\) is the unsmoothed observed-data clamp target from \cref{obj:def:clamp-functional}.
\end{lemmav}

\begin{lemmav}{lem:stabilized-risk-upper}[Stabilized risk upper bound]
Assume that the declared constants satisfy
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Strata.)} \(J\geq 1\).
\item \textbf{(Smoothness and thinning.)} \(\beta>0\) and \(\kappa\geq 0\).
\item \textbf{(Model radii.)} \(L>0\), \(c_->0\), \(c_-\leq \kappa+1\leq c_+\), and \(p_{\min}>0\) with \(p_{\min}\leq 1/J\).
\item \textbf{(Threshold and calibration.)} \(0<\bar\delta<1\) and \(0<\alpha<1/2\).
\end{itemize}
Then there is a constant \(C_{\mathrm{up}}>0\), depending on these declared constants, such that the following holds.  For every deterministic threshold sequence \((\delta_n)_{n\geq 1}\) with \(0\leq \delta_n\leq \bar\delta\) for every \(n\), and for every deterministic split sequence \(B_{\bullet}=(B_n)_{n\geq 1}\) in which each \(B_n=(I_{0,n},I_{1,n},I_{2,n})\) consists of pairwise disjoint subsets of \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\) with
\[
|I_{0,n}|\geq \lfloor n/4\rfloor,\qquad
|I_{1,n}|\geq \lfloor n/4\rfloor,\qquad
|I_{2,n}|\geq \lfloor n/4\rfloor,
\]
there is \(N<\infty\) such that, for every \(n\geq N\),
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M}
\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}
\left|\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{TG}}_{n,B_n}-\theta_{\delta_n}(P)\right|
\leq
C_{\mathrm{up}}\left(n^{-1/2}+\delta_n^{\kappa+1}h_n^\beta\right),
\]
where \(\mathcal M\) is the model class in \cref{obj:def:model-class}, \(\theta_{\delta_n}(P)\) is the clamp target in \cref{obj:def:clamp-functional}, \(\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{TG}}_{n,B_n}\) is the total-Gram estimator in \cref{obj:def:total-gram-estimator}, \(h_n\) is the information-balance bandwidth for \(\delta_n\) in \cref{obj:def:bandwidth}, and the rate is the frontier in \cref{obj:def:frontier}.
\end{lemmav}

\begin{lemmav}{lem:bandwidth-phases}[Bandwidth phase bounds]
There exist constants \(c_{\mathrm{bal}},C_{\mathrm{bal}},c_{\mathrm{far}},C_{\mathrm{far}}\) with
\[
0<c_{\mathrm{bal}}\le C_{\mathrm{bal}},
\qquad
0<c_{\mathrm{far}}\le C_{\mathrm{far}},
\]
such that the following assertions hold.  Let
\[
\delta_{\mathrm{edge},n}
=
n^{-1/(2\beta+\kappa+1)} .
\]
For every \(J\), every observed law \(P\), every \(L,c_-,c_+,p_{\min},\alpha\), and every deterministic sequence \((\delta_n)_{n\ge1}\), suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Regime constants.)} \(J\ge1\), \(\beta>0\), \(\kappa\ge0\), \(L>0\), \(c_->0\), \(c_-\le \kappa+1\le c_+\), \(p_{\min}>0\), \(p_{\min}\le 1/J\), \(0<\bar\delta<1\), and \(0<\alpha<1/2\).
\item \textbf{(Thinning.)} The law \(P\) satisfies the polynomial thinning condition in \cref{obj:ass:polynomial-thinning} with exponent \(\kappa\) and constants \(c_-,c_+\).
\item \textbf{(Thresholds.)} \(\delta_n\in[0,\bar\delta]\) for every \(n\).
\end{itemize}
Let \(h_n\) be the information-balance bandwidth from \cref{obj:def:bandwidth} for \((n,\delta_n,\beta,\kappa,\bar\delta)\).  Then, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
c_{\mathrm{bal}}
\le
n h_n^{2\beta+1}(\delta_n+h_n)^\kappa
\le
C_{\mathrm{bal}},
\]
and
\[
c_{\mathrm{bal}}h_n^{-2\beta}
\le
n h_n(\delta_n+h_n)^\kappa
\le
C_{\mathrm{bal}}h_n^{-2\beta}.
\]
If \(\delta_n/\delta_{\mathrm{edge},n}\to\infty\), then, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
c_{\mathrm{far}}\bigl(n\delta_n^\kappa\bigr)^{-1/(2\beta+1)}
\le
h_n
\le
C_{\mathrm{far}}\bigl(n\delta_n^\kappa\bigr)^{-1/(2\beta+1)} .
\]

Moreover, for every \(D>0\), there exist constants \(c_{\mathrm{near}},C_{\mathrm{near}}\), depending on \(D\), with
\[
0<c_{\mathrm{near}}\le C_{\mathrm{near}},
\]
such that, under the same regime-constant, thinning, and threshold conditions, if
\[
|\delta_n|\le D|\delta_{\mathrm{edge},n}|
\]
for all sufficiently large \(n\), then, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
c_{\mathrm{near}}n^{-1/(2\beta+\kappa+1)}
\le
h_n
\le
C_{\mathrm{near}}n^{-1/(2\beta+\kappa+1)} .
\]
\end{lemmav}

\begin{lemmav}{lem:total-gram}[Total Gram stabilization]
Let \(J\) be a positive integer and let the declared constants satisfy
\[
\beta>0,\qquad \kappa\ge 0,\qquad L>0,\qquad
0<c_-\le \kappa+1\le c_+,\qquad
0<p_{\min}\le 1/J,\qquad
0<\bar\delta<1,\qquad 0<\alpha<1/2 .
\]
Then there are constants \(C,c>0\), depending only on these declared constants, such that the uniform population Gram lower-bound constant \(\lambda_\star\) in \cref{obj:def:local-design-notation}, evaluated at \((\ell,\kappa,c_-,c_+)\) with \(\ell=\lceil\beta\rceil-1\), satisfies \(\lambda_\star>0\), and the following hold.

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Model and sampling.)} \(P\in\mathcal M\) as in \cref{obj:def:model-class}, and \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are sampled according to \cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling}.
\item \textbf{(Split and threshold.)} \(I_0,I_1,I_2\subset\{1,\ldots,n\}\) are deterministic, pairwise-disjoint split blocks with \(|I_b|\ge \lfloor n/4\rfloor\) for \(b=0,1,2\), and \(\delta\in[0,\bar\delta]\).
\item \textbf{(Bandwidth and stratum.)} \(h_n\) is the information-balance bandwidth from \cref{obj:def:bandwidth} at \((n,\delta,\beta,\kappa,\bar\delta)\), and \(x\in\mathcal X\).
\end{itemize}

For the good-design event \(\Omega_x\) in \cref{obj:def:local-design-notation},
\[
P^{\otimes n}(\Omega_x^c)
\le
C\exp\{-c\,n\,h_n(\delta+h_n)^\kappa\}.
\]
On \(\Omega_x\), the exact local-polynomial intercept weights \(w_{ix}\) in \cref{obj:def:local-design-notation} satisfy, for every \(j=0,\ldots,\ell\),
\[
\sum_{i\in I_2} w_{ix} U_i^j
=
\begin{cases}
1, & j=0,\\
0, & j\ge 1,
\end{cases}
\]
and also obey
\[
\sum_{i\in I_2}|w_{ix}|\le C,
\qquad
\sum_{i\in I_2}w_{ix}^2\le \frac{C}{N_x}.
\]
\end{lemmav}

\begin{lemmav}{lem:continuity-regression-extension-unique}[Unique continuous regression extension]
Let \(J\) be a positive integer, let \(\kappa,c_-,c_+,p_{\min},\bar\delta\in\mathbb R\), and let \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}\) be a continuity-only observed clamp model with these constants, as in \cref{obj:def:continuity-model-class}. Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Design constants.)} The constants satisfy
\[
0\leq \kappa,\qquad
0<c_-,\qquad
c_-\leq \kappa+1\leq c_+,\qquad
0<p_{\min}\leq \frac1J,\qquad
0<\bar\delta<1 .
\]
\item \textbf{(Continuous versions.)} For \(r=1,2\), \(\mu_r:\mathcal X\times\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) satisfies that \(a\mapsto \mu_r(x,a)\) is continuous on \([0,\bar\delta]\) for every \(x\in\mathcal X\).
\item \textbf{(Regression version property.)} For \(r=1,2\),
\[
\mathbb E_P[Y\mid X,A]=\mu_r(X,A)
\quad\text{\(P\)-almost surely.}
\]
\end{itemize}
Then, for every \(x\in\mathcal X\),
\[
\mu_1(x,a)=\mu_2(x,a)
\qquad\text{for every }a\in[0,\bar\delta].
\]
\end{lemmav}
